author: ericirby
body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Add GitHub Actions to run Claude Code on @claude mentions and to auto-review pull requests.
> 
> - **GitHub Actions**:
>   - `/.github/workflows/claude.yml`:
>     - Triggers on issue/PR review comments and issues; filters for `@claude` mentions.
>     - Grants permissions (incl. `actions: read`) and runs `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1` with `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`.
>   - `/.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml`:
>     - Triggers on `pull_request` `opened`/`synchronize`.
>     - Runs `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1` with a review prompt targeting code quality, bugs, performance, security, and tests.
>     - Restricts tools via `claude_args` to selected `gh` commands; includes optional author filters (commented).
>

# Pull Request

## Description

Reduces HF breach → tx broadcast latency on Base (no mempool) via predictive queueing, pre-computed plans, hedged RPC reads, and optimized gas pricing. Target: <450ms decision latency, ≥60% cache hit rate.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] Performance improvement
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes)
- [ ] Test coverage improvement

## Related Issues

Fixes #

## Changes Made

### Core Services (6 new files, +697 LOC)

**HedgedProvider** (`execution/HedgedProvider.ts`)
- Races primary RPC vs secondary after `HEAD_CHECK_HEDGE_MS` delay
- First response wins; applies to `getUserAccountData`, multicalls
- Metrics: `hedgeFiredTotal`, `hedgeWinnerSecondary`

**PreSimCache** (`services/PreSimCache.ts`)
- LRU cache keyed by `(user, debtAsset, collateralAsset, blockTag)`
- 2-block TTL, 1000 entry default capacity
- Metrics: `preSimCacheHit/Miss`, `preSimLatencyMs`

**GasLadder** (`services/GasLadder.ts`)
- Pre-computed fast/mid/safe tip ladder (5/3/2 Gwei defaults)
- Synchronous `getGasPlan()` - no RPC latency on critical path
- Updates per block from `baseFee + tip`

**AllowanceChecker** (`services/AllowanceChecker.ts`)
- Startup + periodic checks for USDC/EURC/WETH/cbETH approvals
- Dry-run by default (`APPROVALS_AUTO_SEND=false`)
- Logs `[approvals] ok|needed token=...`

### Service Enhancements

**RealTimeHFService** (+77 LOC)
```typescript
// Track ΔHF/Δblock (N=4 observations)
private updateHfDeltaTracking(user, hf, block, debtUsd) {
  // Compute slope, project HF_next
  if (projectedHf < PRE_SIM_HF_WINDOW && debtUsd >= MIN_DEBT_USD) {
    this.preSimQueue.set(user, { projectedHf, debtUsd, ... });
    console.log(`[pre-sim] queued user=...`);
  }
}
```

**PriceService** (+45 LOC)
```typescript
// Per-block price coalescing
async getPriceAtBlock(symbol: string, blockTag: number): Promise<number> {
  const key = `${symbol}-${blockTag}`;
  if (cached) return cached.price;
  // ... resolve + cache + metric
}
```

**ExecutionService** (+21 LOC)
- Lazy-init `PreSimCache` and `GasLadder` when enabled
- Fast-path: check cache before full plan recompute

### Configuration (9 new env vars)

```bash

PRE_SIM_HF_WINDOW=1.01              # Queue threshold
PRE_SIM_MIN_DEBT_USD=100            # Minimum to qualify
PRE_SIM_CACHE_TTL_BLOCKS=2          # Cache validity

GAS_LADDER_ENABLED=true             # Default on
GAS_LADDER_FAST_TIP_GWEI=5          # Competitive
GAS_LADDER_MID_TIP_GWEI=3           # Normal
GAS_LADDER_SAFE_TIP_GWEI=2          # Non-urgent

APPROVALS_AUTO_SEND=false           # Safe default

SECONDARY_HEAD_RPC_URL=https://...  # Optional hedge
HEAD_CHECK_HEDGE_MS=300             # Hedge delay
```

author: just-cameron
body:
## Summary

Makes `--new` flag safer by default. Previously it would nuke ALL memory blocks (including persona/human), which was too destructive.

## The Problem

The old `--new` behavior:
```bash
letta --new  # Creates agent with brand new persona, human, project, skills blocks
```

This meant:
- ❌ Your persona gets reset every time
- ❌ Your human context is lost
- ❌ No shared state between agents
- ❌ Too destructive for "I just want a new agent"

## The Solution

Split into two flags:

### `--new` (Safe)
```bash
letta --new  # NEW: Reuses global blocks (persona/human), new local blocks
```

✅ Creates new agent  
✅ Keeps your persona/human blocks  
✅ Creates new project/skills blocks  
✅ Safe for experimentation  

### `--fresh-blocks` (Nuclear)
```bash
letta --fresh-blocks  # OLD --new behavior
```

🔥 All blocks fresh  
🔥 Complete isolation  
🔥 No shared state  

## Examples

```bash
# Want to experiment? Use --new (keeps your identity)
letta --new

# Want complete isolation? Use --fresh-blocks
letta --fresh-blocks

# Want to resume? Just use letta (unchanged)
letta
```

## Breaking Change

If you relied on `--new` creating completely isolated agents, use `--fresh-blocks` instead.

Most users will prefer the new safer behavior.

## Testing

- ✅ All 335 tests pass
- ✅ Lint passes
- ✅ Type check passes
- ✅ Help text updated

author: copilot
body:
Modernize aging codebase: replace synchronous diesel/r2d2 with diesel-async/deadpool, update all dependencies to latest stable versions, and simplify to essential user management structure.

## Database Layer
- **diesel-async 0.7.4** with deadpool connection pooling replaces r2d2
- All repository methods now async/await
- Connection pool type: `Pool<AsyncPgConnection>`

```rust
// Before: sync with r2d2
pub fn find_by_id(&self, user_id: Uuid) -> Result<User, AppError> {
    let conn = &mut self.pool.get()?;
    users.find(user_id).first(conn)?
}

// After: async with deadpool
pub async fn find_by_id(&self, user_id: Uuid) -> Result<User, AppError> {
    let mut conn = self.pool.get().await?;
    users.find(user_id).get_result(&mut conn).await?
}
```

## Dependencies
- actix-web 4.3 → 4.11
- jsonwebtoken 8.3 → 10.2 (added rust_crypto features)
- bcrypt 0.14 → 0.17, thiserror 1.0 → 2.0
- dotenvy 0.15 (replaces deprecated dotenv)

## Schema Simplification
- Single `users` table: `id`, `email`, `full_name`, `password?`, timestamps
- Removed articles, comments, favorites, follows, tags, profiles
- Fresh migration in `migrations/2024-11-15-000000_create_users/`

## Architecture
- Preserved `AppError` pattern with HTTP response mapping
- Maintained clean feature structure: `app/features/user/{entities, repository}`
- Simplified DI container to user repository only
- Removed auth middleware (restore as needed)
- Simple healthcheck at `/api/healthcheck`

Build verified, ready for incremental feature additions.

author: esmeralda-rg
body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive monthly attendance reporting feature to the backend. It adds endpoints for generating paginated attendance reports, monthly summaries, and exporting attendance data in PDF and CSV formats. The implementation includes new DTOs, repository queries, and service methods for data aggregation and report generation, along with the necessary security configuration updates.

**Attendance Reporting and Export Functionality**

* Added endpoints in `AttendanceController` for:
  - Paginated monthly attendance reports (`/api/attendances/report`)
  - Monthly attendance summaries (`/api/attendances/report/summary`)
  - Exporting attendance reports in PDF (`/api/attendances/report/pdf`) and CSV (`/api/attendances/report/csv`) formats
* Implemented service methods in `AttendanceService` to:
  - Aggregate monthly attendance data per user
  - Generate PDF reports with attendance tables and a bar chart of monthly totals
  - Generate CSV reports including annual attendance summaries
* Introduced DTOs `AttendanceReportDTO` and `AttendanceSummaryDTO` for structured report data [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e354715a86a83848ee70313ff95045cc6b742c9c668c546454a4045c06f2fb8eR1-R17) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-10b7581b2bd58230ee917ec46af514be08ce6a59abc3e8f8da94ea868645cc00R1-R15)

**Repository Enhancements**

* Added custom JPA queries in `AttendanceRepository` to:
  - Retrieve attendances for a specific year and month, with pagination
  - Count attendances by user, year, and month
  - Count total attendances per month

**Security Configuration**

* Updated `SecurityConfig` to allow `ADMIN` and `MONITOR` roles access to the new attendance reporting endpoints

**Supporting Changes**

* Added necessary imports for PDF, CSV, and image/chart generation in `AttendanceService`
* Minor import additions in `AttendanceController` for pagination, HTTP headers, and media types [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-15e04ee54b15f572f82d701b187e7105d2855f7f1e5381fd6ba1bf907c81a8a7R3-R4) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-15e04ee54b15f572f82d701b187e7105d2855f7f1e5381fd6ba1bf907c81a8a7R16-R22)

author: trentanater77
body: Refactor Firebase usage for prompts and recordings to fix auth warnings, enable background recording uploads, and resolve spark persistence issues. The "prompts" Firebase instance was causing "Provided authentication credentials for the app named 'prompts' are invalid" warnings and WebSocket connection failures due to an attempt to establish a full RTDB connection when only REST access was needed. This PR removes the redundant initialization and treats it as a REST-only dependency. Recording uploads were blocking the UI and failing if the user navigated away, which is now addressed by using `keepalive: true` for metadata writes and robust upload state tracking. Spark persistence was also failing due to incorrect query parameters, which is now fixed by using proper URL encoding and query construction. ---

author: kevin-courbet
body:
## Description

Fixes a critical bug in PostgreSQL unique constraint introspection that causes `drizzle-kit push` to falsely detect missing constraints even when they exist in the database.

## Problem

The current introspection query at `pgSerializer.ts:1230-1236` uses `information_schema.constraint_column_usage` which creates a **Cartesian product** when joined with the `columns` table:

```sql
JOIN information_schema.constraint_column_usage AS ccu USING (constraint_schema, constraint_name)
JOIN information_schema.columns AS c ON c.table_schema = tc.constraint_schema
  AND tc.table_name = c.table_name AND ccu.column_name = c.column_name
```

This returns **zero rows** for multi-column unique constraints, causing `drizzle-kit push` to prompt users to add constraints that already exist.

## Solution

Replace `constraint_column_usage` with `key_column_usage` (the standard PostgreSQL information_schema table for PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE constraints) and properly join on:
- `constraint_name`
- `constraint_schema`
- `table_name`

Added `ORDER BY kcu.ordinal_position` to preserve column order in multi-column constraints.

## Testing

### Before Fix
```sql
-- Returns 0 rows for multi-column unique constraint
SELECT c.column_name FROM information_schema.table_constraints tc
JOIN information_schema.constraint_column_usage AS ccu USING (constraint_schema, constraint_name)
JOIN information_schema.columns AS c ON c.table_schema = tc.constraint_schema
  AND tc.table_name = c.table_name AND ccu.column_name = c.column_name
WHERE tc.table_name = 'address' AND tc.constraint_type = 'UNIQUE';
-- Result: 0 rows
```

### After Fix
```sql
-- Returns all columns in the constraint
SELECT kcu.column_name FROM information_schema.table_constraints tc
JOIN information_schema.key_column_usage kcu
  ON tc.constraint_name = kcu.constraint_name
  AND tc.constraint_schema = kcu.constraint_schema
  AND tc.table_name = kcu.table_name
WHERE tc.table_name = 'address' AND tc.constraint_type = 'UNIQUE'
ORDER BY kcu.ordinal_position;
-- Result: 5 rows (all columns in the unique constraint)
```

## Impact

- ✅ Fixes constraint detection for ALL multi-column unique constraints
- ✅ Eliminates false "add constraint" prompts in `drizzle-kit push`
- ✅ No breaking changes - only fixes broken introspection
- ✅ Compatible with all PostgreSQL versions

## Related Issues

Closes #4490
Closes #4531
Closes #4921

## Checklist

- [x] Bug fix in drizzle-kit introspection
- [x] Tested with real PostgreSQL database
- [x] No breaking changes
- [x] Commit signed

author: sonicadvance1
body:
Fixes a bug in guest VDSO symbol loading where clang sticks all symbols in to .dynsym where gcc sticks them in to .symtab. Search both. This effectively meant the couple of guest VDSO symbols were always failing to get found, causing us to allocate yet another page on 32-bit. So effectively three pages stolen.

Peeled out of #5039

## Summary
- add a dedicated receiver audio-monitor endpoint, auto-play widget, and error handling so SDR streams can be provisioned and started directly from the settings UI
- surface RBDS/RDS programme metadata, carrier status, and squelch telemetry in both the Icecast metadata pipeline and the radio settings monitor card
- extend radio receiver persistence with squelch configuration defaults, migrations, and tests to keep Raspberry Pi deployments efficient while enabling carrier-loss alarms
- automatically backfill squelch configuration columns when legacy deployments have not yet run the latest Alembic migration so the radio settings UI loads without database errors
- restore SDR audio monitor adapters from their persisted configuration when requests arrive before the controller has them in memory, preventing repeated 503 responses in the settings UI

author: will-ness-ai
body:
## Summary
Fixes the empty results issue when parsing goodwatch.app pages by adding support for JavaScript-rendered content.

## Changes
- ✅ Install Puppeteer for headless browser support
- ✅ Create new `fetcher.ts` module with smart auto-detection
- ✅ Automatically detect client-side rendering (looks for `animate-pulse` or `skeleton` classes)
- ✅ Add `--browser` flag to force headless browser usage
- ✅ Update CLI to use new fetcher module

## How it works
1. First tries fast axios HTTP request
2. If page contains loading skeletons, automatically switches to Puppeteer
3. Waits for JavaScript to render the actual content
4. Successfully extracts all related movies and TV shows

## Testing
Tested with: `pnpm start "https://goodwatch.app/show/66732-stranger-things"`

Successfully extracted:
- 32 movies across 4 categories (Overall, Intrigue, Tension, Mystery)
- 32 TV shows across 4 categories (Sci-Fi, Fantasy, World Immersion, Adrenaline)

All with complete metadata (name, link, image, goodwatch_score).

author: seanchatmangpt
body:
Add comprehensive GitHub Actions management commands to the playground CLI using clap-noun-verb pattern.

**New Commands:**
- `playg gh stat` - Show workflow statistics and status
- `playg gh list` - List all workflows (names, paths, or JSON)
- `playg gh check` - Validate workflows for syntax and best practices
- `playg gh runs` - Show recent workflow runs (requires gh CLI)
- `playg gh open` - Open GitHub Actions page in browser

**Features:**
- Automatic workflow discovery from .github/workflows/
- YAML syntax validation
- Security best practices checks (explicit permissions)
- Deprecated action detection
- JSON output for programmatic use
- Integration with gh CLI for live status

**Validation Rules:**
- Checks for explicit permissions declarations
- Identifies deprecated actions:
  - actions/create-release@v1
  - actions/upload-release-asset@v1
  - actions/cache@v1/v2 (for Rust projects)
- Validates YAML syntax

**Dependencies:**
- Added serde_yaml ^0.9 to playground/Cargo.toml

**Usage Example:**
```bash
# Check status of all workflows
cargo run --bin playg -- gh stat

# Validate workflows
cargo run --bin playg -- gh check

# List workflows
cargo run --bin playg -- gh list

# Show recent runs (requires gh CLI)
cargo run --bin playg -- gh runs --limit 5
```

The implementation follows the existing clap-noun-verb pattern and integrates seamlessly with the playground CLI structure.

body:
## Summary

Add support for Discord MESSAGE_UPDATE events, allowing webhooks to receive notifications when messages are edited or updated.

## Changes

### Configuration (`src/params.rs`)

- Added `MESSAGE_UPDATE_DIRECT` and `MESSAGE_UPDATE_GUILD` environment variables
- Added `has_message_update_events()` helper method

### Bridge Layer (`src/bridge/`)

- Created `MessageUpdatePayload` wrapper for webhook payloads
- Added `handle_message_update()` method to `EventBridge`

### Main Handler (`src/main.rs`)

- Implemented `message_update` event handler
- Updated `build_gateway_intents()` to include MESSAGE_UPDATE events
- Auto-enables MESSAGE_CONTENT intent when MESSAGE_UPDATE is configured

### Documentation

- Updated README.md with MESSAGE_UPDATE event details and payload examples
- Added configuration examples to `.env.example`
- Updated Gateway Intents section with MESSAGE_UPDATE checkmarks

## Implementation Notes

Following the same simple pattern as MESSAGE_DELETE events:

- **No message filtering**: Sender type filtering is not available (MessageUpdateEvent may not include author info)
- **No webhook actions**: Response actions are not supported for update events
- **Partial data**: Discord only provides changed fields in MessageUpdateEvent
- **MESSAGE_CONTENT intent**: Required to receive updated message content

## Webhook Payload

```json
POST {HTTP_ENDPOINT}?handler=message_update

{
  "message_update": {
    "id": "1234567890123456789",
    "channel_id": "9876543210987654321",
    "guild_id": "1111111111111111111",
    "content": "Updated content here",
    "edited_timestamp": "2024-01-15T12:35:00.789Z"
  }
}
```

## Testing

- ✅ All tests pass (77 unit tests, 20 integration tests)
- ✅ cargo check successful
- ✅ cargo clippy --all-targets successful

## Use Cases

- Content moderation (track edited messages)
- Audit logging (who edited what and when)
- Spam detection (rapid edit patterns)

author: copilot
body:
UniFi APs randomize octets when broadcasting multiple BSSIDs (one per SSID), but the randomization can occur in any position, not just the last octet. The existing implementation only matched the first 5 octets, causing failures when middle octets differed.

## Changes

- **Replaced prefix matching with fuzzy octet-by-octet comparison**
  - Old: Match first 10 hex chars (5 octets), assumes last octet varies
  - New: Compare each of 6 octets individually, allow up to 2 to differ in any position
  - Select best match when multiple APs qualify (most octets matching)

```swift
// Before: Only handles last octet differing
let bssidPrefix = String(normalizedBSSID.prefix(10))
return accessPoints.first { ap in
    String(ap.normalizedMAC.prefix(10)) == bssidPrefix
}

// After: Handles any octet differing
var matchingOctets = 0
for i in stride(from: 0, to: 12, by: 2) {
    let bssidOctet = normalizedBSSID[i..<i+2]
    let apOctet = ap.normalizedMAC[i..<i+2]
    if bssidOctet == apOctet { matchingOctets += 1 }
}
// Match if ≥4 of 6 octets match
```

Fast path (exact match) preserved. Maintains O(n) complexity.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

## ✉️ PR 제목
feat: 편지 기능 구현

---

## 📌 작업 개요
사용자의 감정/상황을 기록할 수 있는 **편지(Letter) 기능**을 구현했습니다.  

- 편지 작성(Create)
- 단건/목록 조회(Read)
- 수정(Update)
- 삭제(Delete)

---

## 🛠 주요 개발 내용

### 1️⃣ Letter 엔티티
- `Letter`
  - `id`
  - `user` (작성자, User 엔티티 FK)
  - `to`
  - `from`
  - `content` (내용)
  - `createdAt`, `updatedAt`

---

### 2️⃣ 편지 작성 API
- `POST /api/letters`
- 요청 DTO: `LetterCreateRequest`
- 현재 로그인한 사용자 정보로 작성자 매핑
- 검증 실패 시 예외 처리 (`@Valid` 등)

---

### 3️⃣ 편지 조회 API
#### 🔹 단건 조회
- `GET /api/letters/{letterId}`
- 본인 글인지 검증 후 조회

#### 🔹 목록 조회
- `GET /api/letters`
- 현재 로그인한 사용자가 작성한 Letter 목록 반환
- *(선택)* 최신순 정렬

---

### 4️⃣ 편지 수정 API
- `PUT /api/letters/{letterId}`
- 요청 DTO: `LetterUpdateRequest`
- 작성자 본인인지 검증 후 수정
- `updatedAt` 갱신

---

### 5️⃣ 편지 삭제 API
- `DELETE /api/letters/{letterId}`
- 작성자 본인인지 검증

---

author: natthapolvanasrivilai
body:
## Summary

Adds Redis and RabbitMQ infrastructure to support MALIEV microservices event-driven architecture and distributed caching requirements.

## Infrastructure Components

### Redis (04-redis)
- **Purpose**: Distributed caching for microservices
- **Image**: `redis:7.2-alpine`
- **Configuration**:
  - Single instance StatefulSet
  - 512Mi memory limit with LRU eviction at 256MB
  - 1Gi persistent volume
  - Cache-only mode (persistence disabled)
- **Service Endpoint**: `redis.maliev-infra.svc.cluster.local:6379`
- **Health Checks**: TCP socket and redis-cli ping

### RabbitMQ (06-rabbitmq)
- **Purpose**: Message broker for event-driven architecture
- **Image**: `rabbitmq:3.12-management-alpine`
- **Configuration**:
  - Single instance StatefulSet
  - 1Gi memory limit with 60% high watermark
  - 5Gi persistent volume
  - Management UI and Prometheus metrics enabled
- **Service Endpoints**:
  - AMQP: `rabbitmq.maliev-infra.svc.cluster.local:5672`
  - Management UI: `rabbitmq.maliev-infra.svc.cluster.local:15672`
- **Default Credentials**: maliev/maliev123 (should be changed via External Secrets in production)
- **Health Checks**: rabbitmq-diagnostics ping and port connectivity

## Invoice Service Configuration

Updated Invoice Service deployment to use the new infrastructure:

### Production Environment
- Enabled Redis connection: `redis.maliev-infra.svc.cluster.local:6379`
- Enabled RabbitMQ connection with full configuration
- Added environment variables for service discovery

### Development Environment
- Same configuration as production for consistency
- Allows testing event-driven features in development

## Deployment Order

1. **Deploy Infrastructure First** (ArgoCD should sync these first):
   - `1-cluster-infra/04-redis`
   - `1-cluster-infra/06-rabbitmq`

2. **Then Deploy/Update Services**:
   - `3-apps/maliev-invoice-service` (and other services as needed)

## Verification Steps

After deployment:

1. **Verify Redis**:
   ```bash
   kubectl get statefulset -n maliev-infra redis
   kubectl get svc -n maliev-infra redis
   kubectl exec -n maliev-infra redis-0 -- redis-cli ping
   ```

2. **Verify RabbitMQ**:
   ```bash
   kubectl get statefulset -n maliev-infra rabbitmq
   kubectl get svc -n maliev-infra rabbitmq
   kubectl port-forward -n maliev-infra svc/rabbitmq 15672:15672
   # Visit http://localhost:15672 (maliev/maliev123)
   ```

3. **Verify Invoice Service**:
   ```bash
   kubectl get pods -n maliev-dev -l app=maliev-invoice-service
   kubectl logs -n maliev-dev -l app=maliev-invoice-service | grep -E "Redis|RabbitMQ"
   ```

## Impact

- **Invoice Service**: Will now have distributed caching and event consumption capabilities
- **System Health**: Resolves unhealthy deployment status caused by missing infrastructure
- **Scalability**: Enables horizontal scaling with shared state via Redis
- **Event-Driven**: Enables microservices to communicate via RabbitMQ events

## Related PRs

- [ ] Maliev.InvoiceService PR (to be created) - Updates appsettings.Production.json

## Notes

- Infrastructure is deployed to `maliev-infra` namespace
- Services use cluster DNS for discovery
- Default RabbitMQ credentials should be rotated in production
- Redis runs in cache-only mode (no persistence)
- Both services are single-instance (not clustered) - sufficient for current scale

author: pblivingston
body:
## What
Expand and refine the Voicemeeter PowerShell API surface: more parameters/commands on strips and buses, new feature classes (Option, Preset, Fx, Patch), EQ enhancements, VAIO extension support, and Potato Pitch controls. README and CHANGELOG updated.

## Why
- Broader control and parity with Voicemeeter features across variants
- Clearer, less redundant API surface
- Groundwork for future VMRAPI additions (e.g., presets)

## Key additions and changes

- Bus
  - Bus[i].sel (select strip gainlayers with Strip[i].gain)
  - Bus[i].monitor (Monitor On Select)
  - Bus[i].vaio on physical buses (VAIO extension)

- Strip
  - Strip[i].audibility (Voicemeeter Basic)
  - Strip[i].vaio on physical strips (VAIO extension)
  - Strip[i].denoiser.threshold
  - EQ gains on virtual strips: bass/low, mid/med, treble/high
  - Karaoke alias: Strip[i].karaoke for Strip[i].k
  - Pitch (Potato) via new Pitch class:
    - Strip[i].Pitch.on, .drywet, .pitchvalue, .loformant, .medformant, .hiformant

- Commands, Buttons, and Recorder
  - Command.save($filepath), Command.reset
  - Button[i].color (write-only, via Command.Button[i].color)
  - Recorder.eject (via Command.eject)
  - README now mentions Recorder.replay and Recorder.gain

- New classes and API structure
  - Preset class (foundation for store/overwrite, name/comment, load/save); Preset[i].recall implemented
  - Fx class: Reverb.on/ab; Delay.on/ab
  - Patch class: asio[i], OutA2[i]–OutA5[i], composite[i], insert[i], postFaderComposite, postFxInsert
  - Option class:
    - sr, asiosr, delay[i]
    - Buffer: mme, wdm, ks, asio
    - Mode: exclusif, swift
    - monitorOnSel, sliderMode
  - New IRemote and IndexedIRemote base classes to consolidate remote/setter/getter/etc.
  - Alternate gainlayer pattern supported: Strip.gainlayer[i] (existing pattern still works)

- EQ enhancements (Bus.Eq and Strip.Eq)
  - Eq.save($filename), Eq.load($filename)
  - Eq.Channel[i].Cell[j].{on,type,f,gain,q}

### Changes
- Strip[i].limit is now float (GUI truncates visually, value is not actually integer)
- Strip[i].mono is alias for Strip[i].mc on virtual strips (aligns with Python module)
- GainLayers now based on KindMap (only added for Potato)
- Strip and Bus now use IndexedIRemote base class

### Removed
- Bus[i].limit from README (does not exist)

### Fixed
- MacroButton index range in README
- Parenthesis in Strip.AppMute string
- Vban.stream.sr variable corrected (`$this._port` → `$this._sr`)

## Notes / compatibility
- Mostly additive; one potential surface change: Strip[i].limit type changed to float.
- CHANGELOG ([Unreleased]) and README are updated.

## Remaining before Ready for review
- [x] Update/expand tests for new features
- [x] Run tests and investigate/resolve failures
  - [x] All boolean tests pass
  - [x] All integer tests pass
  - [x] All float tests pass
  - [x] All string tests pass
  - [x] All fade tests pass
  - [x] All eq tests pass
  - [x] All special tests pass
- [x] Cleanup/streamline to reduce redundancy
- [x] Re-run tests and finalize docs

## Questions for reviewers
- Are the new parameter/command names and structure acceptable?
- New/adjusted aliases (e.g., mono → mc on virtual, karaoke for k, bass/low, mid/med, treble/high): okay? Any you’d like removed or added?
- Changing Strip[i].limit to float: okay? Is a migration note needed?
- Preset/Fx/Patch/Option/IRemote/IndexedIRemote: class names and placement okay?

author: copilot
body:
## Fix Playhead Visual and Audio Sync Issues and Grid Window Switcher

### Problem Statement
The Bloops application had two critical issues:
1. **Playhead visual and audio sync** - The playhead visual position was not synchronized with audio playback
2. **Grid window switcher** - Did not display the proper number of windows and did not update correctly when changing grid zoom

### Root Cause Analysis

#### Issue 1: Playhead Desync
**Location:** `Grid.svelte` line 336  
**Problem:** `playheadStepInWindow = playheadStep % visibleColumns`  
This calculated the playhead position using modulo without considering which window was being displayed. When viewing window 2, 3, or 4, the playhead would appear at the wrong position.

**Fix:** `playheadStepInWindow = playheadStep - windowOffset`  
Now correctly calculates position relative to the current window offset.

#### Issue 2: Window Switcher 
**Location:** `Grid.svelte` line 178  
**Problem:** `totalWindows = Math.ceil(displayColumns / visibleColumns)` where `displayColumns === visibleColumns`  
This always resulted in 1 window regardless of zoom level.

**Root cause:** The `visibleColumns` calculation was incorrect:
```javascript
// OLD (incorrect)
const displayColumns = Math.floor((logicalColumns * zoom) / stepsPerBarSafe);
const visibleColumns = displayColumns;
```

**Fix:** Simplified to use zoom level directly:
```javascript
// NEW (correct)
const visibleColumns = Math.min(zoomLevel, logicalColumns);
const totalWindows = Math.ceil(logicalColumns / visibleColumns);
```

### Changes Made

#### 1. Fixed visibleColumns Calculation (`Grid.svelte`)
**Before:** Complex formula that produced incorrect results  
**After:** `visibleColumns = Math.min(zoomLevel, logicalColumns)`

This ensures:
- Zoom level 8 → 8 visible columns → 4 windows (for 32-step project)
- Zoom level 16 → 16 visible columns → 2 windows
- Zoom level 32 → 32 visible columns → 1 window
- Zoom level 64 → 32 visible columns → 1 window (clamped to project length)

#### 2. Fixed totalWindows Calculation (`Grid.svelte`, line ~171)
**Before:** `Math.ceil(displayColumns / visibleColumns)` → always 1  
**After:** `Math.ceil(logicalColumns / visibleColumns)` → correct count

#### 3. Fixed Playhead Position (`Grid.svelte`, line ~329)
**Before:** `playheadStep % visibleColumns`  
**After:** `playheadStep - windowOffset`

#### 4. Updated Coordinate Calculations Throughout
- Removed complex `displayColumns` calculations
- Simplified all coordinate mappings to work directly with logical columns
- Fixed: note rendering, inactive note rendering, pointer event handling, keyboard navigation

#### 5. Added Window Clamping on Zoom Change (`App.svelte`)
```javascript
const handleZoomChange = (event) => {
  const oldZoom = zoomLevel;
  zoomLevel = event.detail.level;
  
  // Recalculate and clamp manual window when zoom changes
  if (manualWindow !== null && oldZoom !== zoomLevel) {
    const oldVisibleCols = Math.min(oldZoom, columns);
    const currentLogicalPos = manualWindow * oldVisibleCols;
    const newVisibleCols = Math.min(zoomLevel, columns);
    const newWindow = Math.floor(currentLogicalPos / newVisibleCols);
    const maxWindow = Math.max(0, Math.ceil(columns / newVisibleCols) - 1);
    manualWindow = Math.min(newWindow, maxWindow);
  }
};
```

#### 6. Updated Test Expectations (`Grid.layout.spec.js`)
Fixed test to match new visibleColumns logic - correctly expects 8 visible columns at zoom level 8.

### Testing

#### Automated Tests
✅ 77 tests passing (0 failures related to changes)  
✅ Build succeeds without errors  
✅ No security vulnerabilities detected (CodeQL)

#### Manual Testing Results
| Test Case | Expected | Actual | Status |
|-----------|----------|--------|--------|
| Zoom 8 | 8 columns, 4 windows | 8 columns, 4 windows | ✅ |
| Zoom 16 | 16 columns, 2 windows | 16 columns, 2 windows | ✅ |
| Zoom 32 | 32 columns, 1 window | 32 columns, 1 window | ✅ |
| Window navigation | Changes grid content | Changes grid content | ✅ |
| Follow mode toggle | Auto/manual switching | Works correctly | ✅ |
| Zoom during manual window | Window adjusts proportionally | Window adjusts correctly | ✅ |

### Screenshots

#### Initial State (Zoom 16, Window 1/2)
![Initial state showing zoom 16 with 16 columns and 2 windows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cadb1069-9588-443e-b449-458a0665fa28)

#### Zoom 8 (Window 1/4)
![Zoomed out to 8 columns, now showing 4 windows total](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5c9a0d45-76f2-40f5-a0f6-0acd5eb22701)

#### Window Navigation (Window 2/4)
![Navigated to window 2, showing different grid section](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/72c774bc-2735-49c4-ad95-0d935885c530)

#### Back to Zoom 16 (Window 1/2)
![Zoomed back in to 16 columns, correctly showing 2 windows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a0b738b-62c8-4d3d-a2f7-f2e55a7397ae)

### Security Summary
✅ No security vulnerabilities detected by CodeQL analysis  
✅ All coordinate calculations use safe bounds checking  
✅ No unsafe DOM manipulation or XSS risks introduced

### Implementation Checklist
- [x] Explore repository and understand code structure
- [x] Identify root causes of playhead sync issue
- [x] Identify root causes of window switcher issues
- [x] Fix playhead visual sync calculation
- [x] Fix totalWindows calculation for window switcher
- [x] Fix visibleColumns to vary by zoom level
- [x] Ensure window state updates correctly on zoom change
- [x] Update test expectations to match new logic
- [x] Build application successfully
- [x] Run existing test suite (77 tests passing)
- [x] Manually test zoom functionality
- [x] Manually test window navigation
- [x] Manually test follow mode
- [x] Take screenshots of UI changes
- [x] Run CodeQL security analysis
- [x] Complete final verification

### Files Changed
- `bloops_app/src/components/Grid.svelte` - Core grid rendering and window logic
- `bloops_app/src/App.svelte` - Zoom change handler with window clamping
- `bloops_app/src/__tests__/Grid.layout.spec.js` - Updated test expectations

### Impact
This fix resolves critical UX issues where:
1. Users experienced visual/audio desync during playback
2. The window switcher was non-functional, showing only 1 window
3. Zoom changes didn't properly update the grid view

The application now provides a smooth, synchronized experience with proper window switching at all zoom levels.

body:
Original flavor campaign options stored random portrait preferences as ordinal based Integer[] array. It relied on the ordinals remaining the same. When I wrote CO IIC this couldn't be changed as it would break existing saves.

Unfortunately, a side effect of this situation is that we cannot have non-combat, non-support professions in the middle of combat & support professions. Otherwise campaign options breaks.

When we fully retired the old vehicle crew professions, a day or two ago, we suddenly had non-combat, non-support professions in the middle of combat & support professions. Calamity ensues.

author: copilot
body:
The `multi-agent-spawner.yml` workflow spawns up to 3 agents in parallel using matrix strategy. Each spawn process updated `.github/agent-system/metadata/last_spawn.txt`, causing Git merge conflicts on concurrent pushes.

## Changes

**Eliminated concurrent writes to shared metadata file:**
- Removed `last_spawn` update from `add_agent_to_registry.py` - individual spawns now only modify their own agent files
- Created `update_last_spawn.py` - called once by workflow after all parallel spawns complete
- Updated `multi-agent-spawner.yml` summary job to run centralized timestamp update

**Fixed metadata handling in distributed mode:**
- `registry_manager.py`: Changed `update_metadata_field()` and `get_metadata()` to prioritize metadata mode over agent mode
- Ensures atomic field updates work correctly when metadata is distributed but agents are in legacy mode

**Testing:**
- Added `test_last_spawn_fix.py` with 4 test cases covering concurrent spawn scenarios

## Pattern

```python
# Before: Concurrent writes → conflicts
spawn_1: update_agent() + update_last_spawn()  # ↘
spawn_2: update_agent() + update_last_spawn()  # → CONFLICT
spawn_3: update_agent() + update_last_spawn()  # ↗

# After: Serial write for shared metadata
spawn_1: update_agent()  # ✓
spawn_2: update_agent()  # ✓
spawn_3: update_agent()  # ✓
summary: update_last_spawn()  # ✓ Single atomic update
```

This eliminates the race condition while preserving timestamp accuracy.

author: brandtkeller
body:
## Description

Migrates Zarf package signing to the Sigstore bundle format, aligning with Cosign v3 standards and improving signature portability and verification capabilities.

## Changes

The signing implementation now defaults to `NewBundleFormat: true` and generates both legacy signature files and the new bundle format (saved as `zarf.bundle.sig`). The `SignPackage()` function automatically configures the bundle path through the BundlePath option, ensuring all signing operations produce both formats for backward compatibility. 

Verification logic implements a fallback strategy that prefers the bundle format over legacy signatures. When verifying packages, the system first checks for a bundle file, and if not found, falls back to the legacy signature format with a deprecation warning to inform users of the transition. Validation Package integrity checks now exclude bundle files from validation, treating them similarly to how legacy signature files are handled to prevent false validation errors. 

The implementation maintains dual format support by generating both bundle and legacy signatures during signing operations. This enables a graceful migration path where verification prefers the modern bundle format but seamlessly falls back to legacy signatures with appropriate warnings. The bundle format is now enabled by default, aligning Zarf with Cosign v3 standards.

The bundle format significantly improves verification capabilities by including timestamps and transparency log entries, which enables verification of packages signed with short-lived certificates even after expiration. Existing packages with legacy signatures remain fully functional while new signatures automatically use the modern format. This sets the foundation for eventually deprecating legacy signature support.

## Related Issue

Fixes #4296
Fixes #4276

- [x] Test, docs, adr added or updated as needed
- [x] [Contributor Guide Steps](https://github.com/zarf-dev/zarf/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#developer-workflow) followed

body:
#### PR Classification
Comprehensive refactor to modernize the ProGUI codebase, improve maintainability, and introduce structured error handling.

#### PR Summary
This pull request refactors the legacy ProGUI codebase by encapsulating global state into classes, introducing modern C++ practices, and adding structured error handling. It also includes unit tests and updates the design documentation.
- **CMakeLists.txt**: Updated to include new source files and dependencies (OpenGL, MuJoCo).
- **ProGuiChain.cpp/h**: Introduced `ProGuiChain` class for chain management, including cube operations, direction history, and gap layout updates.
- **ProGuiSim.cpp/h**: Added `ProGuiSim` class for simulation and rendering logic, including physics options and camera controls.
- **ProGuiUI.cpp/h**: Refactored UI handling into `ProGuiUI` class, supporting input events and file I/O capture.
- **Result.h**: Added `Result` type for structured error handling with a `Status` enum and factory methods.

author: wolfgangs
body:
This adds a schema document and a validation method for PR's to make sure that the `lsl_definitions.yml` follows the so far agreed schema.

It uses [Yamale](https://github.com/23andMe/Yamale) to perform the validation, which is installed by adding it as a requirement to the existing pyproject

There is also a small change to the config for the pre-commit action, as yamale uses multi-document yaml files for its validation method, so the pre-commits yaml check, needs to allow for this.

It also inclides 1 small change to the lsl_definitions.yml, to standardize a function, to match the rest, for the schema

Now, all initial workflow versions are marked as active, allowing users to:

2. Edit an empty workflow to add nodes
3. Create new versions if needed

This aligns with the import_workflow logic which also auto-activates the first version when a workflow has no active version.

Fixes: Workflow selection issue for newly created workflows

author: mgazza
body:
## Summary

Adds timing instrumentation to track planning cycle execution duration and Intelligent Octopus Go charge action latency.

## Changes

### Planning Execution Time Tracking (`plan.py`)
- Records planning cycle duration in `plan_last_duration_seconds` attribute
- Logs planning execution time for visibility
- Useful for monitoring system performance and detecting slow planning cycles

### IOG Charge Action Timing (`execute.py`)
- Tracks time from IOG charge slot start to when charge command is sent
- Records latency in `iog_last_action_latency_seconds` attribute
- Only records when `octopus_intelligent_charging` is enabled
- Filters out stale data (> 10 minutes)
- Sets action status to track success/failure

## Use Case

These attributes can be read by monitoring plugins (e.g., Prometheus metrics exporters) to:
- Track planning cycle performance over time
- Monitor responsiveness of charge actions
- Identify performance degradation
- Set up alerting for slow operations

## Testing

- [ ] Planning duration is logged after each planning cycle
- [ ] IOG latency is recorded when charge windows are set
- [ ] Attributes are available for external monitoring tools

body:
## Summary

Updates production configuration to enable Redis and RabbitMQ infrastructure that is now available in the cluster.

## Changes

### appsettings.Production.json

**Redis Configuration:**
- **Before**: `"Configuration": ""` (in-memory fallback)
- **After**: `"Configuration": "redis.maliev-infra.svc.cluster.local:6379"`
- **Impact**: Enables distributed caching across service instances

**RabbitMQ Configuration:**
- **Before**: `"Enabled": false` (in-memory MassTransit)
- **After**: 
  ```json
  {
    "Enabled": true,
    "Host": "rabbitmq.maliev-infra.svc.cluster.local",
    "Port": 5672,
    "Username": "maliev",
    "Password": "maliev123",
    "VirtualHost": "/"
  }
  ```
- **Impact**: Enables event-driven architecture and payment event consumption

## Dependencies

This PR requires infrastructure to be deployed first:
- ✅ **GitOps PR**: https://github.com/MALIEV-Co-Ltd/maliev-gitops/pull/50
- Must deploy Redis and RabbitMQ to `maliev-infra` namespace before merging this PR

## Deployment Order

1. **First**: Merge and deploy maliev-gitops#50 (infrastructure)
2. **Second**: Merge and deploy this PR (service configuration)

## Benefits

### Redis Distributed Cache
- Enables horizontal scaling with shared state
- Improves performance with distributed caching
- Reduces database load

### RabbitMQ Event-Driven Architecture
- Consumes payment events from Payment Service
- Automatically links payments to invoices
- Decouples services via asynchronous messaging

## Health Check Behavior

With infrastructure available:
- **Liveness**: Always 200 OK
- **Readiness**: 
  - 200 OK (Healthy) - all components available
  - 200 OK (Degraded) - Redis unavailable (falls back to in-memory)
  - 503 (Unhealthy) - Database unavailable

## Testing

After deployment:
1. Verify Redis connection in logs
2. Verify RabbitMQ consumer registration in logs
3. Create a payment in Payment Service
4. Verify invoice status updates automatically

## Related PRs

- Infrastructure: maliev-gitops#50
- Previous config: #11 (merged - disabled RabbitMQ)

## Notes

- Environment variables in GitOps deployment override appsettings.json values
- Both development and production environments configured to use infrastructure
- Credentials are placeholder - should be managed via External Secrets in production

author: juangallardo19
body:
Problema:
- El método removePlayerById() no llamaba a transferLeadership()
- Solo hacía players.remove(player) directamente
- Resultado: El liderazgo se "transfería" al mismo usuario que estaba saliendo
- El usuario que quedaba en la sala no podía hacer nada (no era líder)

Solución:
- removePlayerById() ahora llama a removePlayer() en lugar de players.remove()
- removePlayer() maneja correctamente la transferencia de liderazgo:
  1. Primero REMUEVE al jugador de la lista
  2. Luego verifica si era líder y llama a transferLeadership()
  3. transferLeadership() asigna players.get(0) que YA NO incluye al jugador que salió

Flujo correcto:
removePlayerById(playerId) → removePlayer(player) →
  players.remove(player) → transferLeadership() →
  players.get(0) = nuevo líder (diferente al que salió)

body:
## Description

Implements granular, group-based permission system replacing simple admin/user roles. Provides 28 default permissions across 8 resources with four-layer admin lockout prevention.

## Motivation & Context

Multi-user deployments require fine-grained access control. The existing binary admin/user role system cannot express "user can manage clients but not delete users" scenarios. This blocks production deployments needing compliance-ready audit trails and least-privilege access patterns.

## Implementation Details

### Database Schema
- **Permission model**: `(resource, action)` tuples with unique constraint. Actions: read, create, update, delete, download
- **UserGroup extensions**: Added `is_admin` boolean (auto-grants all perms) and `updated_at` timestamp
- **Association tables**: `user_group_permissions` (groups↔permissions), `user_group_memberships` (users↔groups)

### Seeded Defaults
- 28 permissions: clients, groups, firewall_rules, ip_pools, ca, users, lighthouse, dashboard
- "Administrators" group (`is_admin=True`): system group, cannot be deleted/modified
- "Users" group: read-only permissions across all resources
- Auto-migration: existing admin users → Administrators group

### API Endpoints (12 new)
**Permissions**: `GET /api/v1/permissions`

**User Groups**: CRUD + `member_count`/`permission_count` aggregates
```python
GET    /api/v1/user-groups
GET    /api/v1/user-groups/{id}
POST   /api/v1/user-groups
PUT    /api/v1/user-groups/{id}
DELETE /api/v1/user-groups/{id}
```

**Membership**: `GET|POST|DELETE /api/v1/user-groups/{id}/members[/{user_id}]`

**Permission Grants**: `GET|POST|DELETE /api/v1/user-groups/{id}/permissions[/{perm_id}]`

### Permission Checking
```python
# Dependency injection pattern
from app.core.auth import require_permission

@router.get("/clients")
async def list_clients(
    user: User = Depends(require_permission("clients", "read")),
    session: AsyncSession = Depends(get_session)
):
    # 403 if user lacks permission
    ...

# Programmatic checks
if await user.has_permission(session, "clients", "delete"):
    # User in admin group OR has explicit permission via group membership
    ...
```

### Admin Lockout Prevention
Four enforcement layers (all return 409 Conflict):
1. `DELETE /user-groups/{administrators_id}` → blocked
2. `PUT /user-groups/{administrators_id} {"is_admin": false}` → blocked
3. Remove last member from Administrators → blocked
4. Delete last user in Administrators → blocked

### Migration
Alembic revision `f40acab05062`:
- Creates `permissions` table (String type for SQLite compat, not Enum)
- Adds `is_admin`, `updated_at` to `user_groups` via `ALTER TABLE`
- Seeds all default data in transaction
- Idempotent: safe to re-run

### Backward Compatibility
`require_admin()` now checks admin group membership instead of role. Zero breaking changes.

### Code Changes
- `app/models/permissions.py`: Permission model, UserGroup extensions
- `app/models/user.py`: `has_permission()` async method
- `app/core/auth.py`: `require_permission()` factory, updated `require_admin()`
- `app/routers/api.py`: 12 endpoints + admin deletion safeguards
- `app/models/schemas.py`: Pydantic models for request/response
- Removed duplicate user-groups endpoints (lines 1772-2143)

## Screenshots (if applicable)

N/A - Backend API only. Frontend integration separate effort.

## Checklist
- [x] I have tested these changes locally (manual integration tests: all 12 endpoints, lockout prevention verified)
- [x] I have updated documentation as needed (PERMISSIONS_SYSTEM.md, PERMISSIONS_QUICKSTART.md, test_permissions_manual.md)
- [x] I have added/updated tests as needed (manual test suite confirms functionality)
- [ ] I have assigned reviewers

As an administrator, I want to create user groups and assign granular permissions to those groups so that I can control access to features across the Managed Nebula platform while preventing admin lockout.

## Acceptance Criteria

### 1. Permission Model
- [ ] Create a `Permission` model with fields:
  - `id` (UUID primary key)
  - `resource` (string): The resource type (e.g., "clients", "groups", "firewall_rules", "ip_pools", "ca", "users", "lighthouse", "dashboard")
  - `action` (enum): One of `read`, `create`, `update`, `delete`, `download`

## Redesign Security & Privacy Page for Keyturn Studio

### Plan:
- [ ] Understand current site structure and design patterns
- [ ] Create new content for secure.html following the 8-section structure
- [ ] Implement hero section with clear messaging
- [ ] Add "What we actually need" section with minimal requirements list
- [ ] Add "Optional access" section
- [ ] Add "What we never touch" section (EMR/EHR exclusions)
- [ ] Add "How we handle access" section with security practices
- [ ] Add "Data & tracking" section
- [ ] Add "For clinic clients" subsection
- [ ] Add "Questions or concerns?" closing section
- [ ] Update page metadata (title, description)
- [ ] Test the page locally to ensure it works properly
- [ ] Take screenshot of the redesigned page

### Approach:
- Keep existing header, footer, and visual design patterns
- Reuse card components, buttons, and typography from styles.css
- Maintain dark/premium theme consistent with the rest of the site
- Use calm, honest, reassuring tone (not legalese)
- Focus on minimal access requirements and transparent practices

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

You are editing the **Security & Privacy** page for my studio site “Keyturn Studio”.

Context:
- Tech: static HTML + CSS, dark/premium theme consistent with the rest of the site.
- We work primarily with **clinics** (dental, implant, cosmetic, medspa, physio, chiro, spa) and **boutique hotels & inns**.
- In reality, most projects only require a few simple things: domain/DNS access, content/assets, and a place to send visitors (phone, email, booking link). Access to other systems is optional, not mandatory.
- Tone: calm, honest, reassuring, NOT legalese. No fake “HIPAA compliant™” claims.

Your job:
- Keep the existing header, nav, footer, and overall visual style (cards, headings, spacing).
- Rewrite and restructure the **main content** so it reflects a simple, realistic security model.
- Emphasise:
  - We usually need *very little* access to start.
  - We stay well away from EMR/EHR and medical records.
  - We’re happy to work with their IT/compliance person if they have one.

Please reshape the page into the following sections (reuse existing components where possible):

1) Hero
- H1: something like “Security & privacy that stays out of your medical records.”
- Subline: one sentence explaining that we only work with public-facing website and marketing tools, not internal clinical systems.

2) What we actually need for most projects
- Short paragraph explaining that, for a typical clinic or inn, we can launch a new site with just a few items.
- Bulleted list labelled “For most projects, we only need:” with items like:
  - Domain / DNS access (or help from your current IT person) so we can point your domain to the new site.
  - Basic content and assets: logo, photos, services/treatments, contact details, opening hours.
  - A phone number, email, and/or booking link so visitors know how to book or request a consult.
- Make it clear this is the **usual minimum**, not a long list of heavy integrations.

3) Optional access (only if you want deeper help)
- Intro sentence: “Sometimes, you may choose to give us access to more tools so we can set things up properly for you. These are optional, not required to start.”
- Bulleted list of optional items:
  - Website host / CMS (if we’re editing an existing site instead of replacing it).
  - Booking or scheduling system dashboard (only if you want us to embed/adjust widgets or booking flows).
  - Analytics and tag tools (Google Analytics, Tag Manager, call tracking) to set up tracking and simple reports.
- Include a one-liner that we prefer user accounts/invites over shared passwords.

4) What we never touch
- Heading like “What we don’t access”.
- Clear bullets:
  - No EMR/EHR systems.
  - No patient medical records or clinical notes.
  - No insurance or billing systems.
  - No cardholder data or internal payment systems (beyond embedding your existing checkout/booking widgets).
- Add a short sentence: “Your marketing website should not be the place where detailed medical records live. We can help route enquiries into whatever secure systems you already use.”

5) How we handle access
- A short section describing simple, common-sense practices:
  - Least-privilege access: we request just enough access to do the job.
  - Preference for individual user accounts or admin-invited access, rather than sharing the main login.
  - Credentials stored in an encrypted password manager on our side.
  - You can revoke our access at any time; after launch, we’re happy to have you remove our accounts if you prefer.
- Present these as 3–4 clean bullets or small cards.

6) Data & tracking on your site
- Explain, in plain language:
  - We track pageviews, button clicks, and form submissions to understand what works.
  - Tracking is configured on analytics properties that **you own**.
  - We don’t sell or share your analytics data with other clients.
  - We avoid heavy ad-tech/remarketing scripts by default unless you specifically ask for them.

7) For clinic clients specifically
- Short subsection that reiterates:
  - We work on your **public marketing site**, not your medical record systems.
  - We recommend keeping enquiry forms simple (contact details + “reason for visit”) and routing anything more sensitive into your existing secure systems.
  - If you have an IT or compliance contact, we’re happy to work with them to fit your policies.

8) Questions or concerns?
- Closing strip with one sentence like: “If you or your IT team have questions about how we handle access, just ask.”
- A single button or link: “Email us about security” using the existing contact email or route.

General rules:
- Make the page feel like a relaxed but competent explanation, not a wall of legal text.
- Emphasise that starting a project with us does **not** require handing over your whole digital stack — just a few essentials, plus optional extras if you want deeper help.
- Keep typography and layout consistent with the rest of the site; only the text and section headings should change.

</details>

author: josephsavona
body:
I've been trying out LLM agents for compiler development, and one thing i found is that the agent naturally wants to run `yarn snap <pattern>` to test a specific fixture, and I want to be able to tell it (directly or in rules/skills) to do this in order to get the debug output from all the compiler passes. Agents can figure out our current testfilter.txt file system but that's just tedious. So here we add support for `yarn snap -p <pattern>`. If you pass in a pattern with an extension, we target that extension specifically. If you pass in a .expect.md file, we look at that specific fixture. And if the pattern doesn't have extensions, we search for `<pattern>{.js,.jsx,.ts,.tsx}`. When patterns are enabled we automatically log as in debug mode (if there is a single match), and disable watch mode.

Open to feedback!

author: conorbronsdon
body:
Problem: GitHub Actions workflow failing with error: "Dependencies lock file is not found in /home/runner/work/..."

Root cause: package-lock.json was in .gitignore, preventing the actions/setup-node@v4 cache feature from working.

Solution:
- Remove package-lock.json from .gitignore
- Commit package-lock.json to repository

Benefits:
- Enables npm dependency caching in CI (faster builds)
- Ensures reproducible builds across environments
- Best practice for production applications

This fixes the deployment workflow failure.

author: dj-ccs
body:
The Cesium Ion default imagery fails due to COEP restrictions on the internal worker files (transferTypedArrayTest.js, createVerticesFromHeightmap.js). This causes the globe to be invisible even though it exists for interaction.

Solution: Always use OpenStreetMap as the primary imagery provider instead of relying on Cesium Ion, which requires additional COEP configuration.

Fixes: Black screen issue where globe ellipsoid exists but has no visible texture

author: copilot
body:
### **User description** The Export Console Logs feature fails because `browser.downloads.download()` returns immediately while Firefox performs async I/O (1-10s with `saveAs: true`). The blob URL was revoked after 1s via `setTimeout()`, causing downloads to fail when Firefox tried to read the already-revoked URL. ## Changes **popup.js (lines 135-152)** - Replace Blob URL with base64-encoded Data URL - Remove `setTimeout()` cleanup (unnecessary for Data URLs) - Data URLs are immune to revocation timing issues **Before:** ```javascript const blob = new Blob([logText], { type: 'text/plain;charset=utf-8' }); const blobUrl = URL.createObjectURL(blob); await browser.downloads.download({ url: blobUrl, filename, saveAs: true }); setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(blobUrl), 1000); // Race condition ``` **After:** ```javascript const base64Data = btoa(unescape(encodeURIComponent(logText))); const dataUrl = `data:text/plain;charset=utf-8;base64,${base64Data}`; await browser.downloads.download({ url: dataUrl, filename, saveAs: true }); // No cleanup needed - data is inline ``` **.gitignore** - Add `coverage/` directory **docs/implementation-summaries/** - Add comprehensive implementation summary with Mozilla Bug #1271345 reference ## Notes Data URL approach is suitable for log files (<10MB). For larger files, would need event-driven blob revocation via `downloads.onChanged` listener.

Make sure to fully read the .md document, identify the issues, figure out what's causing the issues, and implement the changes described in the .md document while making sure that the rest of the extension is in full working order.

## Compose Comprehensive Requirements Documents for Business Verticals

Based on the architectural observation that **atomicity peaks at the ERP core** while **business verticals demand cohesive bounded contexts**, I will create comprehensive requirements documents for:

### Plan Checklist:

- [x] Understand the architectural context from SYSTEM ARCHITECHTURAL DOCUMENT.md
- [x] Understand the RDP (Reusable Decoupled Package) principle from ATOMICITY-REPURPOSE.md
- [x] Identify existing placeholder files
- [ ] Delegate to Laravel ERP expert to compose nexus-procurement requirements
- [ ] Delegate to Laravel ERP expert to compose nexus-project-management requirements  
- [ ] Delegate to Laravel ERP expert to compose nexus-manufacturing requirements
- [ ] Review generated requirements for consistency and completeness
- [ ] Ensure all documents follow the architectural principles

### Key Architectural Principles to Apply:

1. **Progressive Disclosure**: Start simple, grow within the vertical
2. **Cohesive Bounded Contexts**: Verticals embed domain-specific rules
3. **RDP Philosophy**: Each package must be a "Reusable Decoupled Package" - usable standalone with Play Mode
4. **Statutory Coupling**: Accept that verticals need region-specific logic (e.g., MY PCB rates, tender processes)
5. **Data Ownership**: Related data stays together (e.g., supplier management + tender states in procurement)

### Approach:

Using the Laravel ERP expert agent to ensure:
- Domain-driven design principles
- Contract-driven architecture
- Enterprise-grade best practices
- Proper bounded context definition
- Integration points with core packages (tenancy, audit, workflow, settings)

> <issue_title>Compose Requirement Documents</issue_title>
> <issue_description>Atomicity peaks at the ERP core (tenancy, audit, workflow, settings) because they are shared infrastructure—pure, reusable, zero business logic.
> As packages move outward to business verticals (HRM, Payroll, Procurement), they must embed domain-specific rules (PCB tables, leave policies, 3-way matching). These cannot be fully decoupled without losing coherence.
> At the vertical edge, atomicity breaks because:
> 1.  Statutory coupling – MY PCB rates change yearly; can’t defer to core.
> 2.  Workflow specificity – Procurement needs tender states, not generic workflow.
> 3.  Data ownership – Employee salary + tax reliefs belong together, not split across packages.
> Conclusion: Atomicity serves the core. Verticals demand cohesive bounded contexts. Force-fitting atomicity here creates anemic models and integration hell. Progressive disclosure still applies—start simple, grow within the vertical—but not via atomic micro-packages.
> 
> Based on this understanding, think about how this project adapts to such observation. Then formulate a comprehensive requirements document for nexus-procurement (Nexus\Procurement), nexus-project-management (Nexus\Project) and nexus-manufacturing (Nexus\Manufacturing)</issue_description>

author: vcpmark
body:
The game was freezing during asset loading at "loading legs" or "loading bullet"
because the TextureLoader had no timeout mechanism. If an image failed to load
or took too long, the Promise would hang indefinitely.

Changes:
- Add 10-second timeout to image loading in TextureLoader
- Prevent infinite hangs by rejecting the promise on timeout
- Clean up image resources when timeout occurs
- Optimize asset loading to be parallel instead of sequential
- Improve error handling and diagnostic messages

This ensures the game will always complete loading (with fallbacks if needed)
rather than freezing indefinitely.

author: toyamarinyon
body:
### **User description** # Modularize Giselle into independent packages ## Overview This PR implements a major architectural refactoring to decouple the Giselle core engine from framework-specific implementations. The monolithic `@giselles-ai/giselle` package has been split into multiple focused packages, enabling clearer separation of concerns, independent versioning, and better reusability across different runtime environments. ## ⚠️ Breaking Changes ### Package Reorganization - **React client**: `@giselles-ai/giselle/react` → `@giselles-ai/react` - `useGiselleEngine()` → `useGiselle()` - **Next.js adapter**: `@giselles-ai/giselle/next-internal` → `@giselles-ai/nextjs/internal` - `NextGiselleEngine` → `NextGiselle` - **HTTP router**: `@giselles-ai/giselle/http` → `@giselles-ai/http` - `createJsonRouters` → `jsonRoutes` - `createFormDataRouters` → `formDataRoutes` - **Storage drivers**: `@giselles-ai/giselle` → `@giselles-ai/storage` - **Logger types**: → `@giselles-ai/logger` - **Stream types**: → `@giselles-ai/stream` - **Workspace utilities**: → `@giselles-ai/workspace-utils` ### Core API Changes - `GiselleEngine` → `Giselle` (factory) - `GiselleEngineContext` → `GiselleContext` - Functions now accept `GiselleContext` instead of `GiselleEngineContext` ### Dependency Requirements - Several packages now require `zod` as a peer dependency ### Behavior Changes - `updateWorkspace` no longer triggers Next.js `revalidatePath` internally (callers must handle explicitly) ## Changes ### New Package Structure - **`@giselles-ai/giselle`**: Slimmed-down core engine with runtime modules promoted to top-level folders - **`@giselles-ai/react`**: React hooks, providers, and client utilities - **`@giselles-ai/nextjs`**: Next.js adapter and context helpers - **`@giselles-ai/http`**: HTTP router and handler utilities - **`@giselles-ai/storage`**: Storage interfaces and drivers (fs/memory) - **`@giselles-ai/logger`**: Logger types and noop implementation - **`@giselles-ai/stream`**: Shared stream event schemas for SSE - **`@giselles-ai/workspace-utils`**: Workspace graph and grouping utilities ### Application Updates - Updated playground and studio apps to use new package imports - Standardized engine instance naming to `giselle` across all apps - Studio actions now explicitly handle revalidation after workspace updates - Next.js integration uses `after()` for generation index patch flush ### Internal Improvements - Clearer boundaries between runtime, framework, and infrastructure layers - Shared stream event types between server and client - Consistent API naming conventions ## Testing - All existing tests pass with updated imports - Manual testing completed for: - Playground app functionality - Studio app workflows - Act streaming with new SSE implementation - Storage driver operations - Next.js integration endpoints ## Review Notes - Please pay special attention to the breaking changes section as this will require migration for all consumers - The package split strategy aims to minimize coupling - feedback on package boundaries is welcome - Consider if any additional exports should be included in the new packages for completeness ## Related Issues This refactoring enables future work on: - Independent versioning of packages - Framework-agnostic core engine usage - Improved tree-shaking and bundle size optimization ___ ### **PR Type** Enhancement, Refactoring ___ ### **Description** - **Major architectural refactoring**: Split monolithic `@giselles-ai/giselle` package into 7 focused, independent packages (`react`, `nextjs`, `http`, `storage`, `logger`, `stream`, `workspace-utils`) for better separation of concerns and independent versioning - **Core API normalization**: Renamed factory function `GiselleEngine` → `Giselle`, context type `GiselleEngineContext` → `GiselleContext`, and standardized parameter naming from `giselleEngine` → `giselle` across entire codebase - **Router and hook renaming**: Updated HTTP router functions (`createJsonRouters` → `jsonRoutes`, `createFormDataRouters` → `formDataRoutes`) and React hook (`useGiselleEngine` → `useGiselle`) with corresponding type updates - **Next.js adapter refactoring**: Renamed `NextGiselleEngine` → `NextGiselle` and updated configuration types, with simplified router initialization - **Stream types extraction**: Moved stream event types to dedicated `@giselles-ai/stream` package for shared SSE communication schemas - **Breaking change in workspace updates**: `updateWorkspace` no longer triggers Next.js `revalidatePath` internally; callers must handle explicitly - **Updated all imports**: Migrated 50+ files across apps and packages to use new modular package structure and normalized naming conventions - **Package configuration**: Added `zod` as peer dependency across new packages, created Turbo and TypeScript configurations for all new packages - **Dependency updates**: Updated `package.json` files for playground, studio, and workflow-designer-ui apps to reference new package locations ___ ### Diagram Walkthrough ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Monolithic

author: copilot
body:
## Description

Profiler auto-start was failing silently because `Memory.profiler` initialization happened at module level before the Screeps Memory object was available. This prevented function-level CPU profiling data collection needed for performance optimization.

**Related Issues:** Closes #771

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Automation/workflow improvement
- [ ] Performance optimization
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes)
- [ ] Dependency update

## Changes Made

**Root Cause:** `initProfiler()` called at module level attempted to initialize `Memory.profiler` before Memory object existed, causing auto-start check to fail.

**Solution:** Moved Memory.profiler initialization into `loop()` function where Memory is guaranteed available:

```typescript
// Before: Module level (Memory not available yet)
const profilerInstance = initProfiler(); // Tries to init Memory.profiler

export const loop = (): void => {
  if (__PROFILER_ENABLED__ && !profilerAutoStarted) {
    if (Memory.profiler?.start === undefined) { // Fails if undefined
      profilerInstance.start();
    }
  }
};

// After: Inside loop (Memory available)
export const loop = (): void => {
  if (__PROFILER_ENABLED__ && !profilerAutoStarted) {
    Memory.profiler ??= { data: {}, total: 0 }; // Initialize first
    
    if (Memory.profiler.start === undefined) {
      profilerInstance.start();
      console.log("[Profiler] Auto-started profiler data collection");
      profilerAutoStarted = true;
    }
  }
};
```

**Changes:**
- Moved `Memory.profiler` initialization into `loop()` using nullish coalescing assignment
- Ensures profiler auto-starts on first tick when `__PROFILER_ENABLED__` is true (default)
- Preserves existing profiler data if already initialized

- [ ] End-to-end tests added/updated (`npm run test:e2e`)

author: mattlucian
body:
## Summary
Implement proper ADOT + Axiom integration using a collector.yaml configuration file instead of relying only on environment variables.

## Problem
We've been trying to configure ADOT using only environment variables, but Axiom's official ADOT documentation shows that a **custom collector configuration file** is required.

Reference: https://axiom.co/docs/send-data/aws-lambda-dot

## Solution
Created `packages/functions/src/collector.yaml` with proper ADOT collector configuration:

```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: localhost:4317
      http:
        endpoint: localhost:4318

exporters:
  otlphttp:
    compression: gzip
    endpoint: https://api.axiom.co
    headers:
      authorization: ${env:AXIOM_TOKEN}
      x-axiom-dataset: ${env:AXIOM_DATASET}

service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [otlphttp]
```

## Key Changes

1. **Created collector.yaml** - ADOT collector configuration file
2. **Fixed exec wrapper** - Changed from `/opt/otel-handler` to `/opt/otel-instrument` (correct per Axiom docs)
3. **Added config file env var** - `OPENTELEMETRY_COLLECTOR_CONFIG_FILE: "/var/task/collector.yaml"`
4. **Removed exporter env vars** - `OTEL_EXPORTER_*` variables now in YAML config
5. **Simplified environment** - Only essential variables remain

## Why This Should Work

The ADOT layer needs an explicit collector configuration file to know how to export traces. Environment variables alone are insufficient - the collector reads its configuration from YAML.

Per Axiom's docs, this is the correct way to integrate ADOT with Axiom for Lambda functions.

## Test Plan
- [ ] Deploy to dev
- [ ] Submit contact form
- [ ] Verify NO OTLPExporterError in logs
- [ ] Verify traces appear in Axiom `dev.idevelop.tech` dataset with:
  - HTTP status codes
  - Lambda invocation details
  - AWS service calls (SES, DynamoDB, SSM)

author: dagimassefa
body:
This PR adds new API capabilities to the Chapa Laravel package and updates the CI workflow to ensure compatibility with current development dependencies.

New  Methods

**refund()**
Provides the ability to initiate refunds for a given tx_ref.
Supports optional fields such as reason, amount, reference, and meta.
Integrates with the /v1/refund/{tx_ref} endpoint using Http::withToken().

**getBalance()**
Retrieves the merchant’s account balance.
Accepts an optional currency parameter (ETB, USD, etc.).
Connects to /v1/balances or /v1/balances/{currency} depending on the request.

**CI Workflow Update**

Updated GitHub Actions to run tests on PHP 8.3, which is required by
PHPUnit 11 and Testbench 9.

Resolves Composer dependency conflicts previously occurring with PHP 8.0.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Adds `refund` and `getBalance` methods to `src/Chapa.php` and updates GitHub Actions to run on PHP 8.3.
> 
> - **SDK (`src/Chapa.php`)**:
>   - Add `refund(string $txRef, array $data = [])` to initiate refunds via `POST /refund/{txRef}`.
>   - Add `getBalance(?string $currency = null)` to fetch balances via `GET /balances[/{currency}]`.
> - **CI**:
>   - Update GitHub Actions workflow to use PHP `8.3` in `.github/workflows/workflow_laravel.yml`.

author: leonshimizu
body:
# Add Clerk Authentication & Conversation Management

## 🔐 Authentication
- Integrate Clerk backend SDK for JWT token verification
- Add `verify_user()` middleware for auth token validation
- Update all API endpoints to accept `Authorization` header
- Implement optional authentication (supports both authenticated and anonymous users)
- Add `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` environment variable

## 💾 Database Schema
- Create `conversations` table for user-facing chat management
- Add `user_id` column to `conversation_logs` for user tracking
- Implement soft delete with `deleted_at` column
- Add database indexes for performance optimization
- Create Alembic migrations for schema changes

## 🔄 Conversation Management API
- `POST /api/conversations` - Create new conversation
- `GET /api/conversations` - List user's conversations
- `GET /api/conversations/{id}/messages` - Get conversation history
- `PATCH /api/conversations/{id}` - Update conversation title
- `DELETE /api/conversations/{id}` - Soft delete conversation

## 🚀 Deployment
- Add automatic database migrations on deployment
- Update `render.yaml` with Alembic migration command
- Add `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` and `EMBEDDING_MODE` to environment variables
- Update `requirements.txt` with `alembic` and `clerk-backend-api` dependencies

## 📊 Two-Tier Conversation Tracking
- `conversations` table: User-facing chat management (supports delete)
- `conversation_logs` table: Complete analytics/training data (never deleted)

## 🧪 Testing
- Tested authentication flow with Clerk Development instance
- Verified conversation CRUD operations
- Confirmed soft delete preserves training data
- Tested anonymous user support

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added user authentication system with optional anonymous chat support.
  * Introduced multi-conversation management: users can create, rename, list, and delete conversations.
  * Conversations now persist per user with soft-delete preservation.
  * New Conversation Management API endpoints for CRUD operations.

* **Chores**
  * Added database migration framework.
  * Updated dependencies for authentication and migration support.

* **Documentation**
  * Enhanced guides with authentication and conversation management workflows.

- Replace hardcoded port 0 with dynamically assigned ports using get_available_port()
- Fix SNMP event names: change from snmp_get/snmp_getnext to snmp_request with request_type parameter
- Update event data matching: use "oids" (plural, array) instead of "oid"
- Add server initialization delays (500ms) before SNMP queries
- Export get_available_port() from test helpers for reusability

These changes align the SNMP tests with the actual protocol implementation which uses a single snmp_request event with request_type parameter (GET/GETNEXT) instead of separate event types.
