author: jesseloewen
body:
This pull request introduces major improvements to configuration management and security, shifting all setup to a web interface and adding robust authentication features. It removes the need for manual `.env` or `config.json` editing, centralizes settings in the UI, and implements password and token-based authentication for both app-wide and admin access. The documentation is updated to reflect these changes, making setup and usage clearer for users.

**Configuration & Setup Overhaul:**

- All configuration (API keys, folder paths, AI settings, security, Jellyfin integration) is now managed exclusively through the web interface (`/settings`). Direct editing of `.env` or `config.json` is no longer required or documented. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L5-R31)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L47-R71)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L123-R188)`, `[[4]](diffhunk://#diff-a3046da0d15a27e89f2afe639b25748a7ad4d9290af3e7b1b6c1a5533c8f0a8cL1-L5)`)
- The `.env.example` file and related documentation have been removed, and instructions now direct users to configure everything via the web UI. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a3046da0d15a27e89f2afe639b25748a7ad4d9290af3e7b1b6c1a5533c8f0a8cL1-L5)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L47-R71)`)

**Security & Authentication:**

- Adds optional password protection for the entire app and for the settings page, with secure token-based "remember me" authentication (30-day cookies). Passwords and tokens are managed securely in memory. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-568470d013cd12e4f388206520da39ab9a4e4c3c6b95846cbc281abc1ba3c959L1-R8)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-568470d013cd12e4f388206520da39ab9a4e4c3c6b95846cbc281abc1ba3c959R28)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-568470d013cd12e4f388206520da39ab9a4e4c3c6b95846cbc281abc1ba3c959R38-R220)`, `[[4]](diffhunk://#diff-568470d013cd12e4f388206520da39ab9a4e4c3c6b95846cbc281abc1ba3c959R320-R321)`)
- API keys are masked in the UI (only last 4 digits shown), and authentication tokens are invalidated on password change. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L123-R188)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L280-R327)`)

**Backend & API Changes:**

- The backend now reads API keys and all configuration from the managed settings (not from environment variables), ensuring consistency and security. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-25703fb3f1d8db68b36c0e8bc408539029d990fa9adfb1533bcbc55465e206b6L62-R65)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-25703fb3f1d8db68b36c0e8bc408539029d990fa9adfb1533bcbc55465e206b6L199-R201)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c032948ad7276020e3f393b531ae20e1adf6c3e27a07196a825a97bf45c81a90L613-R606)`)
- Removes support for dry run mode and related code, simplifying file organization logic. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c032948ad7276020e3f393b531ae20e1adf6c3e27a07196a825a97bf45c81a90L377-R379)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c032948ad7276020e3f393b531ae20e1adf6c3e27a07196a825a97bf45c81a90L412-L421)`)

**Documentation Updates:**

- The `README.md` is extensively revised to match the new configuration flow, UI features, and security model. Troubleshooting, usage, and configuration sections are updated for clarity and accuracy. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L5-R31)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L47-R71)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L123-R188)`, `[[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L280-R327)`)

**Web Interface Improvements:**

- The web UI now supports full configuration, secure authentication, and enhanced usability for all major features, including job management, library browsing, logs, and settings. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L123-R188)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L47-R71)`)

These changes modernize the application's setup, improve security, and greatly enhance the user experience.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
fix(02_build_features): Correct "Full/Partial" logic to prevent NaN features

The previous implementation used a fragile duration-based calculation to identify "Full" and "Partial" bars, which failed at day boundaries and caused ~45% of features to be NaN.

This commit replaces the faulty logic with a robust, rule-based approach:
- All RTH bars are now correctly marked as 'Full'.
- Only the last ETH bar of each day is marked as 'Partial'.

This change aligns with the logic described in the research plan and resolves the downstream NaN issue in the feature engineering pipeline.

Fixes #43

author: tqwewe
body:
The `instrument` macro only accepts a literal string for the label field. But this can be quite limiting, and isn't entirely necessary to be restricted to only literal strings.

For example, I am looking to implement support for this crate in kameo, but I can't provide the actor names in the instrument macro with:
```rust
channels_console::instrument!((tx, rx), label = A::name());
```

I *think* this is not a breaking change, so could be a minor/patch version bump.

author: copilot
body:
This PR completes Phase 1 alignment review and Phase 2 development for User Authentication & API Credential Management.

## Phase 1: Schema Alignment (Complete)

Phase 1 implementation review identified three schema mismatches between `price_data_5min` table and ARCHITECTURE.md specification.

**Schema corrections:**
- Primary key: `UUID` → `BIGSERIAL` (50% storage reduction, sequential ordering for time-series)
- Price precision: `DECIMAL(18,8)` → `NUMERIC(20,8)` (headroom for extreme crypto prices)
- Added `created_at` field (audit trail separate from measurement timestamp)

**Code updates:**
- `backend/app/models.py`: Updated `PriceData5Min` model and API schemas
- `backend/app/services/collector.py`: Removed manual UUID generation
- Migration `b5pu1jf8qzda`: Data-preserving upgrade/downgrade path

**Documentation:**
- Added `PHASE1_ALIGNMENT_REVIEW.md` with technical analysis
- Updated `PHASE1_SUMMARY.md` with corrections

## Phase 2: User Authentication & Credential Management (Complete)

Implemented secure credential storage, encryption infrastructure, validation, and comprehensive testing per ARCHITECTURE.md specification.

**User Model Enhancement:**
- Added `created_at` and `updated_at` timestamps to User table
- Added relationship to CoinspotCredentials

**Coinspot Credentials:**
- Created `coinspot_credentials` table with encrypted storage
- Fernet (AES-256) encryption for API keys and secrets at rest
- API key masking in responses (only last 4 characters visible)

**New Services:**
- `backend/app/services/encryption.py`: Fernet encryption service
- `backend/app/services/coinspot_auth.py`: HMAC-SHA512 authenticator for Coinspot API

**API Endpoints:**
- `POST /api/v1/credentials/coinspot` - Create credentials
- `GET /api/v1/credentials/coinspot` - Get credentials (masked)
- `PUT /api/v1/credentials/coinspot` - Update credentials
- `DELETE /api/v1/credentials/coinspot` - Delete credentials
- `POST /api/v1/credentials/coinspot/validate` - Validate credentials against Coinspot API

**Credential Validation:**
- Tests credentials using Coinspot read-only balance endpoint (`/api/v2/ro/my/balances`)
- Updates validation status (`is_validated`) and timestamp (`last_validated_at`) in database
- Comprehensive error handling for authentication, network, and API errors

**Database Migration:**
- Migration `74xslpy3kp6z`: User timestamps and coinspot_credentials table

**Dependencies:**
- Added `cryptography>=42.0.4` (patched for CVE-2024-0727)

**Test Suite (36 tests):**
- `tests/services/test_encryption.py`: 12 encryption service tests (encrypt/decrypt, masking, edge cases)
- `tests/services/test_coinspot_auth.py`: 13 authentication tests (nonce generation, HMAC-SHA512 signing, verification)
- `tests/api/routes/test_credentials.py`: 11 API endpoint tests (CRUD operations, validation, error handling)

## Security

- ✅ CodeQL scan passed (0 vulnerabilities)
- ✅ Dependency vulnerability check passed
- ✅ All credentials encrypted at rest with Fernet (AES-256)
- ✅ API keys masked in responses for security
- ✅ Comprehensive test coverage for security-critical code

## Example

```python
# Phase 1: PriceData5Min Schema Fix
class PriceData5Min(PriceDataBase, table=True):
    id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)  # Auto-increment
    bid: Decimal = Field(sa_column=Column(DECIMAL(precision=20, scale=8)))
    timestamp: datetime = Field(...)
    created_at: datetime = Field(...)  # Audit trail

# Phase 2: User Model Enhancement
class User(UserBase, table=True):
    id: uuid.UUID = Field(default_factory=uuid.uuid4, primary_key=True)
    hashed_password: str
    created_at: datetime = Field(...)  # NEW
    updated_at: datetime = Field(...)  # NEW
    coinspot_credentials: "CoinspotCredentials | None" = Relationship(...)

# Phase 2: Coinspot Credentials
class CoinspotCredentials(CoinspotCredentialsBase, table=True):
    id: uuid.UUID = Field(default_factory=uuid.uuid4, primary_key=True)
    user_id: uuid.UUID = Field(foreign_key="user.id", ondelete="CASCADE")
    api_key_encrypted: bytes = Field(...)  # Encrypted with Fernet
    api_secret_encrypted: bytes = Field(...)  # Encrypted with Fernet
```

All migrations handle existing data safely. Encryption keys should be managed via environment variables or AWS Secrets Manager in production.

- Condensed rendering now clips in Y direction (perpendicular to X-Z plane)
- Removed redundant --orientation argument, clarified -H/--horizontal flag
- Updated help text and examples to reflect vertical as default

The default now creates vertical picture layouts (like walls) matching the VerticalColorBeams.json example, with beams arranged in X-Z grid and Y held constant at -1000.

author: lkwhite
body:
Implements foundation for bulk sample loading via TSV manifest files. This is Phase 1 of a multi-phase implementation.

New Features:
- TSV parser with full error/warning reporting
- Multi-strategy path resolution (absolute, TSV-relative, workspace-relative)
- Sample validation with file existence checks
- Import command UI with preview and confirmation
- Smart loading strategy (eager for small batches, lazy for large)

Files Added:
- src/services/tsv-parser.ts - Parse TSV with validation
- src/services/tsv-path-resolver.ts - Resolve file paths
- src/services/tsv-validator.ts - Validate samples before import
- src/commands/tsv-commands.ts - Import command implementation
- src/services/__tests__/tsv-parser.test.ts - 28 test cases
- docs/TSV_IMPORT_PROGRESS.md - Implementation progress tracking

Files Modified:
- package.json - Added importSamplesFromTSV command
- src/extension.ts - Registered TSV command

Status:
- ✅ Phase 1 Complete: Parsing & validation
- ⚠️ Phase 2 Partial: UI implemented, kernel loading stubbed
- ⬜ Phase 3 Pending: Actual kernel integration
- ⬜ Phase 4 Pending: UI integration (samples panel grouping, session persistence)

Next Steps:
- Implement actual kernel loading in loadSamplesFromTSV()
- Add lazy loading trigger in plot commands
- Add tests for path resolver and validator
- Integrate with Samples panel UI

Related: Addresses future TSV import feature outlined in docs/TSV_IMPORT_FUTURE_DESIGN.md

author: copilot
body:
Implements a Python CLI tool that uses OpenAI GPT-4 Vision to analyze Shopify product variants and propose improved names based on product info and images, with interactive approval before export.

## Implementation

**Core Module** (`variant_renamer.py`)
- CSV parser for Shopify format (handles Options 1-3, variant images, SKUs, pricing)
- `VariantRenamer` class with methods: `load_csv()`, `process_variants()`, `apply_changes()`, `export_csv()`
- AI analysis via OpenAI API: GPT-4o for image-based variants, GPT-4o-mini for text-only
- Interactive CLI workflow with approval gate

**Testing** (15 tests)
- Unit tests for CSV I/O, API integration (mocked), name application
- Integration tests for complete workflow, error handling, data preservation

**Documentation & Examples**
- README, QUICKSTART, and contribution guides
- Sample Shopify CSV with realistic product data
- Package installation support via `setup.py`

## Usage

```python
from variant_renamer import VariantRenamer

renamer = VariantRenamer()
df = renamer.load_csv("products.csv")
proposed = renamer.process_variants(df)  # AI analyzes each variant
renamer.display_proposals(df, proposed)  # Shows current vs proposed
# User approves interactively
df_modified = renamer.apply_changes(df, proposed)
renamer.export_csv(df_modified, "output.csv")
```

Or via CLI:
```bash
variant-renamer products.csv
```

## Security
- Pillow updated to 10.3.0 (fixes buffer overflow + libwebp vulnerabilities)
- CodeQL scan: 0 alerts

- Fixed XSS vulnerability in search results display by using DOM manipulation

## Testing

Tested with malicious input like `<script>alert('XSS')</script>` to ensure XSS is prevented.

## Issues Still Remaining

- Product display still uses innerHTML with unsanitized user content
- LocalStorage still storing sensitive data
- API keys still exposed in frontend code
- Memory leaks from intervals not being cleared

<!-- RECURSEML_SUMMARY:START -->
## High-level PR Summary
This PR addresses XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) vulnerabilities in user input display by replacing unsafe `innerHTML` assignments with secure alternatives. Specifically, it fixes the login success message by using `textContent` instead of `innerHTML`, and secures the search results display by using DOM manipulation methods (`createElement` and `appendChild`) to safely render user-provided content. The PR acknowledges several remaining security and code quality issues that still need to be addressed, including additional XSS vulnerabilities in product display, sensitive data storage concerns, exposed API keys, and memory leaks.

author: gnh1201
body:
Support the file association registration for WelsonJS supported file types

## Summary by Sourcery

Enable file association registration for WelsonJS-supported extensions and extend the launcher to directly handle JS scripts and ZIP packages via a new --file command-line option

New Features:
- Allow the launcher to accept a --file argument to open JS scripts or ZIP packages on startup
- Expose a RunFromZipFile method in MainForm to programmatically launch ZIP packages
- Register a WelsonJS.Script ProgID and associate .js, .ts, .re, .res, .ls, and .coffee files with the launcher in the installer

Enhancements:
- Refactor Program.Main to branch into a HandleTargetFilePath workflow for direct file handling
- Consolidate process input/output streams in RunCommandPrompt for simpler child process execution
- Update MainForm to retain the selected file path and reuse it for ZIP package execution

Build:
- Enable ChangesAssociations in setup.iss and add registry entries for file associations for supported extensions

author: aktarjabed
body:
This commit introduces a comprehensive, optional, and opt-in Cloud AI integration to the NextGenZip application.

- Implements secure, encrypted storage for API keys (`ApiKeyStore`) and cloud configurations (`CloudConfigStore`) using `EncryptedSharedPreferences`.
- Adds a `CloudUsageStore` to track cloud AI usage metrics securely.
- Introduces a multi-provider `CloudAIClient` that supports OpenAI and custom endpoints, with placeholders for Gemini and DeepSeek.
- Implements a new `AdvancedSettingsScreen` with comprehensive controls for managing cloud AI settings, including provider selection, API key management, and a connection test.
- Creates a new `AIChatScreen` that automatically and gracefully falls back to local AI if cloud AI is disabled, not configured, or fails.
- Adds a `CloudUsageDashboard` to display usage metrics and a `TroubleshootingScreen` to help users diagnose common cloud-related issues.
- Updates the `App.kt` to initialize the new secure storage modules on startup.
- Updates the `NavGraph` to include routes for all the new UI screens.
- Adds a `README_CLOUD.md` file to document the new feature.

author: jaskrendix
body:
Changes `RunningEvent`
- added `elapsed_time` to track how long an event has been active
- updated `tick()` to enforce `delay` (wait before start) and `timeout` (cancel after limit)

Changes `EventObject`
- added `timeout` and `delay` fields.  
- TMX events from Tiled remain unchanged, but YAML events can now use these fields
- removed the field validator for a simple ge (priority)

Changes `Priority`
- priority handling has been clarified. Higher numbers now mean higher priority, making the system more intuitive. The evaluation order has been updated so that both global events and local events are sorted by priority in descending order before conditions are checked.

Various:
- `source_type` has been removed from `create_event_object` because unused

author: copilot
body:
Implements functional programming enforcement via [eslint-plugin-functional](https://github.com/eslint-functional/eslint-plugin-functional) to prevent common mutation bugs and encourage immutable patterns.

## Configuration

- **ESLint setup**: `eslint.config.js` with TypeScript support, integrated into `deno task check`
- **Core rules**:
  - `functional/no-let` (error) - enforces `const`
  - `functional/immutable-data` (warn) - prevents mutations, allows accumulator patterns
  - `functional/prefer-readonly-type` (warn) - encourages readonly parameters
  - `functional/no-class-inheritance` (warn) - favors composition
- **Pragmatic exceptions**: Test files and internal tools have relaxed rules

## Code Changes

Refactored to eliminate `let` and imperative patterns:

```typescript
// Before: throttle.ts
let lastCalled = 0
return (...args) => {
  lastCalled = now  // mutation
}

// After: throttle.ts  
const state = { lastCalled: 0 }
return (...args) => {
  state.lastCalled = now  // object property mutation allowed
}
```

```typescript
// Before: levenshtein-distance.ts
const grid: number[][] = []
for (let i = 0; i <= target.length; i++) {
  grid[i] = [i]
  for (let j = 1; j <= source.length; j++) { /* ... */ }
}

// After: functional Array.from
const grid = Array.from({ length: target.length + 1 }, (_, i) => 
  Array.from({ length: source.length + 1 }, (_, j) => /* ... */)
)
```

## Documentation

`FUNCTIONAL_PROGRAMMING.md` covers setup, rules, and rationale for exceptions.

## Result

0 errors, 141 warnings (mostly readonly type suggestions that don't affect runtime behavior).

author: mistercrunch
body:
## Summary

Add comprehensive design doc for a proposed real-time activity feed feature that displays a stream of interesting events happening across boards.

This exploration documents a feature that would reinforce Agor's multiplayer/live identity by making system activity visible and creating awareness of what teammates (and agents) are doing.

## Key Features Proposed

- **Real-time WebSocket event streaming** - Subscribe to interesting events only when feed is open
- **Smart event filtering** - Allowlist of meaningful events (sessions, tasks, worktrees, comments)
- **Ephemeral display** - Append-only, keeps N most recent events (no persistence)
- **Event enrichment** - User context and human-readable summaries
- **Zero performance impact when closed** - Conditional subscription pattern
- **Board-scoped filtering** - Only show events for current board

## Implementation Approach

### Phase 1: Modal Prototype (4-6 hours)
- Create `useActivityFeed` hook with conditional subscription
- Create `ActivityFeedModal` component
- Add badge button in header (next to comments)
- Test with real usage patterns

### Phase 2: Refinement (if valuable)
- Add event filtering controls
- Click-to-navigate to related objects
- Unread badge count
- Persist filter preferences

### Phase 3: Advanced Features (if widely adopted)
- Right sidebar panel (persistent visibility)
- Smart message grouping
- Time-based grouping
- Export activity log

## Why Build This?

1. **Reinforces "aliveness"** - Makes multiplayer aspect visceral
2. **Discovery & awareness** - See what changed, what teammates are doing
3. **Debugging & monitoring** - Understand system activity in real-time
4. **Engagement** - Makes solo work feel less lonely

## Design Doc Location

`context/explorations/activity-feed.md`

## Related Work

- Uses existing WebSocket infrastructure from `context/concepts/websockets.md`
- Aligns with multiplayer features in `context/concepts/social-features.md`
- Complements existing presence, cursors, and comments features

author: teano-uttu-9788
body:
## Summary

This PR launches **H62: Subscription Token Cost Experiment**, a P1 financial hypothesis responding to GG's directive to optimize unit economics by switching from pay-per-token to subscription token billing.

## Hypothesis

**If** we switch from pay-per-token billing to a fixed-rate subscription token model,
**Then** we can reduce cost volatility and maintain the $0.05/call hard guardrail,
**Because** fixed costs eliminate per-call variance.

## Scientific Rigor

**ADSM State:** Hypothesis (H) - Complete definition of all success criteria
**Next Phase:** Phase E (Experiment Setup) - Will be dispatched by ADSM Orchestrator

**Success Criteria (Hard Requirements):**
- Cost per call: ≤$0.05 (hard cap, auto-escalate if exceeded)
- Cost volatility reduction: ≥80% (baseline vs variant)
- Latency P95: ≤5000ms (no degradation)
- Statistical significance: p<0.05 (95% confidence)
- Sample size: n≥30 per group (minimum)

**Guardrails Enforced:**
- Margin floor: 40% minimum (pricing constraint)
- Error rate: <1% timeout, <2% API errors
- Real data only (no mock data)

## Implementation Plan

### Phase E: Experiment Setup (2-3 hours)
- Provision subscription token tier with Google
- Set up A/B test harness
- Prepare metrics collection infrastructure

### Phase X: Execution (4-6 hours)
- Run H59 (Product Agent) with both baseline and variant (30 samples each)
- Run H60 (Sales & Pricing Agent) with both models (30 samples each)
- Collect real execution data

### Phase V: Validation (2-3 hours)
- Two-sample t-test on cost volatility
- Verify all guardrails met
- Generate evidence report

## KIO Framework

After validation, GG will apply KIO (Keep/Integrate/Omit):

| NNP Range | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| ≥0.70 | **KEEP** - Promote to Phase P (production) |
| 0.40-0.69 | **INTEGRATE** - Iterate on model |
| <0.40 | **OMIT** - Revert to pay-per-token |

## Authority & Governance

**Authority:** GG (Lead Strategist)
**ADSM Orchestrator:** Will dispatch Phase E→X→V automatically once this PR merges
**Escalation:** If cost exceeds $0.05/call, auto-escalate to GG
**Correlation ID:** gg-20251115-h62-001

## Test Plan

- [ ] Verify H62 spec loads without errors
- [ ] Confirm baseline model specification complete
- [ ] Confirm variant (subscription token) model specification complete
- [ ] Validate all success criteria are measurable
- [ ] Verify all guardrails are hard constraints
- [ ] Check ADSM phase progression logic

## What Happens Next

1. **Merge This PR** → H62 enters ADSM Hypothesis (H) state
2. **ADSM Orchestrator Reads Team Bus #525** → Detects H62 ready for dispatch
3. **Orchestrator Assigns to CC Session** → Phase E begins (experiment setup)
4. **Automated Progression** → E→X→V phases execute with guardrail enforcement
5. **Validation Complete** → Evidence report generated with exact metrics
6. **GG Decision** → Apply KIO framework (final verdict and action)

## Critical Financial Impact

This experiment directly impacts platform monetization. If successful, the subscription token model becomes the new baseline for all subsequent agents (H63, H64, etc.), reducing operational uncertainty and improving financial predictability.

**Authority:** GG (Lead Strategist)  
**Correlation ID:** gg-20251115-h62-001  
**Mission:** Financial optimization with scientific rigor  
**Status:** Ready for ADSM phase dispatch

기본 폼은 서버 기동 시에 존재하는지 확인하고 초기화하여 생성한다. 

현재 시스템 기본 폼 id를 1이라 가정하고 존재여부를 확인하기 때문에

id가 1인 기본 폼이 삭제됐을 시, 기본 폼을 계속 생성되게 된다. 

따라서 기본 폼에 대한 존재 여부 확인은 name 필드로하여 "시스템 기본 폼" 일 시, 기본 폼을 인식하도록 하였다.

또한 폼 필드에 name과 title이라는 필드는 중복적이기 때문에 name 필드만 쓰기로 하였고

매장에 폼을 할당 할 때, name을 businessName + " 기본 폼" 으로 두었다.

body:
This change fixes a hang in the clustering process that occurred during the river stage. The issue was caused by an attempt to pre-calculate all possible river outcomes, which was computationally infeasible. The fix is to switch to an on-the-fly equity calculation for the river stage, which avoids the hang and makes the clustering process runnable and functionally correct. The clustering settings have also been set to minimal values for faster testing.

author: r33drichards
body:
## Summary
This PR improves the UI to display both tool call inputs (code) and outputs together, especially when executions have errors. Previously, tool calls and their results were displayed as separate, disconnected components, making it difficult to understand what code caused an error.

## Changes Made
- **Merged tool results with tool calls**: Updated `conversationTransform.ts` to match tool results with their corresponding tool calls, so they're displayed together
- **Enhanced ToolCallDisplay component**: 
  - Shows both input and output in a unified, collapsible view
  - Adds visual indicators (icons and color coding) for success/error states
  - Defaults to expanded state so errors are immediately visible
  - Implements smart error detection logic
- **Updated MessageContent**: Simplified to pass merged results to ToolCallDisplay
- **Added comprehensive tests**: New test cases for the merged behavior

## Visual Improvements
- ✅ Green highlighting for successful tool executions
- ❌ Red highlighting for failed tool executions with errors
- 🔽 Expanded by default to show errors immediately
- Clear labels: "Input:", "Output:", and "Error Output:"

## Testing
- Updated existing tests to reflect new behavior
- Added new test case for tool result merging
- All test cases account for the unified display approach

This addresses the user's request to "see the code and outputs on executions with errors too" by making both the tool input and error output visible together in the UI.

author: rz1989s
body:
## Summary
Fixes critical cross-platform compatibility bug where BSD/GNU `stat` command differences caused "syntax error in expression" failures on Linux systems.

## Problem
Issue #57 reported by @polczak-itt on Kubuntu 25.10:
```
/home/piotr/.claude/statusline/lib/security.sh: line 375: 1762957229 - File: "/home/piotr/.cache/claude-code-statusline/cmd_exists_git_piotr_claude_statusline.cache"
...
syntax error in expression (error token is ": \"/home/piotr/.cache/...\"")
```

**Root Cause:**
- `stat -f` (BSD/macOS format) returns **filesystem info** on Linux (not file info)
- Multi-line error output was inserted into bash arithmetic expressions
- Example: `local age=$(($(date +%s) - $(stat -f %m "$file" || stat -c %Y "$file")))`
- On Linux, `stat -f` output polluted the arithmetic context → syntax error

## Solution
Created three platform-aware helper functions in `lib/security.sh`:
- `get_file_mtime()` - Get file modification time (returns Unix timestamp)
- `get_file_permissions()` - Get file permissions (returns octal like "644")
- `get_file_size()` - Get file size in bytes

**Design:**
- Try BSD format first (`stat -f`), then fallback to GNU format (`stat -c`)
- Return clean numeric values with proper error handling
- Prevent stderr pollution in arithmetic contexts
- Fully cross-platform (macOS, Linux, BSD systems)

## Changes
Updated all `stat` command usages across the codebase:
- `lib/security.sh` - 3 locations (permissions check, cache freshness, lock cleanup)
- `lib/cache.sh` - 2 locations (lock age, file size calculation)
- `lib/prayer/location.sh` - 1 location (cache age check)
- `lib/prayer_original_backup.sh` - 1 location (cache age check)

## Testing
- ✅ Security tests pass (cache file handling verified)
- ✅ Statusline works correctly on macOS  
- ⏳ Awaiting Linux testing by @polczak-itt

## Deployment Plan
1. Merge to `nightly` for testing
2. Request @polczak-itt to test on Kubuntu 25.10
3. After confirmation, promote to `main`

Fixes #57

author: pallotron
body:
GitHub's ARM64 runners (ubuntu-latest-arm64) require a paid Team or Enterprise account. The v0.0.1 release succeeded because it had access to these runners, but subsequent releases fail with 404 errors when trying to download the ARM64 provisioner image.

Changes:
- Remove matrix strategy from build-and-release-images job
- Build only AMD64 provisioner image automatically
- Document manual ARM64 build process in docs/release-process.md
- ARM64 images can be built locally on Apple Silicon Macs and uploaded using gh CLI

This approach avoids the 3+ hour ARM64 runner time and eliminates dependency on paid GitHub features while still supporting both architectures.

author: gopimosali
body:
…ctory

Issue:
- Config files were saved in script directory (.laravel-server-config)
- When users clone scripts to different locations, configs aren't found
- Example: server-setup.sh in /root/php-server-setup, but user runs app-setup.sh from ~/php-server-setup

Solution:
- Store configs in system-wide locations:
  * /etc/laravel-server.conf (server config)
  * /etc/laravel-app.conf (app config)
- Both scripts can access configs regardless of where they're run from
- chmod 644 allows all users to read configs
- Backward compatible: app-setup.sh checks old location as fallback

Benefits:
✓ Clone scripts anywhere - configs always accessible ✓ Switch users seamlessly (su - user, then sudo ./app-setup.sh) ✓ Multiple users can run scripts without permission issues ✓ Standard /etc/ location follows Linux conventions

Perfect for the recommended workflow:
1. Run server-setup.sh from anywhere (creates /etc/laravel-server.conf)
2. Switch users: su - username
3. Clone scripts to ~/php-server-setup
4. Run sudo ./app-setup.sh (finds /etc/laravel-server.conf)

author: darshandugar2004
body: This project is a Langflow workflow template that performs **Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)**. Instead of just retrieving information from standard documents, it enhances the process by pulling context from **two different sources**: 1. **A Standard Vector Store (Chroma):** This is used to find relevant unstructured text (like document chunks). 2. **A Knowledge Graph (Neo4j):** This is used to find structured data and relationships (e.g., "Person A *knows* Person B"). By combining both the unstructured text and the structured graph data, the workflow provides a much richer, more accurate context to the language model, allowing it to generate more intelligent and context-aware answers.

author: jenhugu
body:
## 🎯 Enrichissement du modèle ActivityItem

**Objectif** : Enrichir le modèle `ActivityItem` avec de nouveaux champs pour stocker plus d'informations sur les activités et ajouter la gestion d'images via Active Storage.

---

### ✨ Nouveaux champs ajoutés

**Migration créée** : `AddDetailsToActivityItems`

| Champ | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `address` | text | Adresse complète (ex: "15 Rue de Rivoli, 75001 Paris, France") |
| `city` | string | Ville (pour filtrage facile) |
| `country` | string | Pays |
| `opening_hours` | text | Horaires d'ouverture en format texte |
| `duration` | integer | Durée de l'activité en minutes |
| `tagline` | string | Phrase d'accroche courte |

---

### 📸 Active Storage pour les images

**Installation et configuration** :
- Installation d'Active Storage : `rails active_storage:install`
- Migration des tables Active Storage exécutée
- Ajout de `has_one_attached :image` dans le modèle `ActivityItem`

**Stockage** : Local (dans `storage/`) pour le développement. Migration vers Cloudinary possible plus tard si nécessaire.

---

### 🌱 Seeds enrichies

**1. `db/seeds.rb`** - 100 activités parisiennes complètes avec :
- ✅ 30 restos/cafés/bars
- ✅ 25 musées/galeries
- ✅ 20 monuments historiques
- ✅ 15 événements culturels
- ✅ 10 activités sportives/loisirs

Tous les champs sont remplis (`address`, `city`, `country`, `opening_hours`, `duration`, `tagline`, `price`, etc.)

**2. `db/seed_images.rb`** - Script pour attacher automatiquement ~90 images depuis Unsplash

---

### 📋 Commandes exécutées
```bash
rails generate migration AddDetailsToActivityItems
rails db:migrate
rails active_storage:install
rails db:migrate
rails db:seed
rails runner db/seed_images.rb
```

---

### 🚀 Instructions pour l'équipe après le pull

Pour obtenir une base de données propre avec toutes les données :
```bash
# 1. Mettre à jour les dépendances (si nécessaire)
bundle install

# 2. Réinitialiser la base de données
rails db:reset

# 3. Attacher les images aux activités
rails runner db/seed_images.rb
```

**Note** : `rails db:reset` fait automatiquement : drop → create → migrate → seed

---

### 📝 Fichiers modifiés

- `db/migrate/[timestamp]_add_details_to_activity_items.rb` (nouvelle migration)
- `db/migrate/[timestamp]_create_active_storage_*.rb` (migrations Active Storage)
- `app/models/activity_item.rb` (ajout de `has_one_attached :image`)
- `db/seeds.rb` (100 activités parisiennes)
- `db/seed_images.rb` (script d'attachement des images)
- `db/schema.rb` (mis à jour automatiquement)

Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 debug@4.4.2 contains malware after npm account takeover

Impact

On 8 September 2025, the npm publishing account for debug was taken over after a phishing attack. Version 4.4.2 was published, functionally identical to the previous patch version, but with a malware payload added attempting to redirect cryptocurrency transactions to the attacker's own addresses from within browser environments.

Local environments, server environments, command line applications, etc. are not affected. If the package was used in a browser context (e.g. a direct <script> inclusion, or via a bundling tool such as Babel, Rollup, Vite, Next.js, etc.) there is a chance the malware still exists and such bundles will need to be rebuilt.

The malware seemingly only targets cryptocurrency transactions and wallets such as MetaMask. See references below for more information on the payload.

Patches

npm removed the offending package from the registry over the course of the day on 8 September, preventing further downloads from npm proper.

On 13 September, the package owner published new patch versions to help cache-bust those using private registries who might still have the compromised version cached. This version is functionally identical to the previously known-good version, published as a patch version bump above the compromised version.

Users should upgrade to the latest patch version, completely remove their node_modules directory, clean their package manager's global cache, and rebuild any browser bundles from scratch.

Those operating private registries or registry mirrors should purge the offending versions from any caches.

References

  • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/npm-debug-and-chalk-packages-compromised
  • https://socket.dev/blog/npm-author-qix-compromised-in-major-supply-chain-attack
  • https://www.ox.security/blog/npm-packages-compromised/

Point of Contact

In the event suspicious behavior is still observed for the package listed in this security advisory after performing all of the above cleaning operations (see Patches above), please reach out via one of the following channels of communication:

  • Bluesky, package owner: https://bsky.app/profile/bad-at-computer.bsky.social
  • debug repository, tracking issue (applies to all packages affected in the breach): #1005

body:
Modernize portfolio with horizontal layouts for hero/footer, add dark/light mode toggle, and remove professional experience section.

## Changes

### Layout Restructure
- **Hero**: Horizontal flex layout with avatar left, content right (responsive to vertical on mobile)
- **Footer**: Horizontal layout with copyright left, social links right
- **About**: Removed professional experience timeline entirely

### Theme System
- Added dark/light mode toggle in navbar (right of Contact link)
- CSS variables for theme colors with localStorage persistence
- Inline script in `BaseLayout.astro` prevents flash on load

```typescript
// Theme toggle implementation
const getTheme = (): string => {
  if (typeof localStorage !== 'undefined' && localStorage.getItem('theme')) {
    return localStorage.getItem('theme') || 'dark';
  }
  return 'dark';
};

const setTheme = (theme: string): void => {
  if (theme === 'light') {
    document.documentElement.classList.remove('dark');
    // Update icons...
  } else {
    document.documentElement.classList.add('dark');
    // Update icons...
  }
  localStorage.setItem('theme', theme);
};
```

Adds support for the `r` command to represent rests (休符) in MML strings. `c r c` now produces: note C, silence, note C with proper timing.

### Changes

**Tree-sitter grammar** (`tree-sitter-mml/grammar.js`)
- Added `rest` rule matching `/[rR]/`

**Pass 1 - Tokenization** (`src/pass1_parser.rs`)
- Handle `rest` node type, emit rest token

**Pass 2 - AST generation** (`src/pass2_ast.rs`)
- Convert rest tokens to AST nodes with `note_type: "rest"`

**Pass 3 - MIDI events** (`src/pass3_events.rs`)
- Modified all event generation modes (sequential, multi-channel, chord)
- Rests advance time by duration without generating note_on/note_off events

**Tests** (`tests/test_rest.rs`)
- Added comprehensive test coverage for rest functionality across all passes

### Example

```rust
// Input: "c r c"
// Pass 1: [note(c), rest(r), note(c)]
// Pass 2: [note{pitch:60}, rest{}, note{pitch:60}]
// Pass 3: [
//   note_on(60, t=0),    note_off(60, t=480),
//   // rest here - no events, time advances
//   note_on(60, t=960),  note_off(60, t=1440)
// ]
```

body:
Text in the reading panel was cut off on the right side because the MarkdownViewer was not using full available width.

### Changes

**Initial Fix:**
- Set `HorizontalAlignment = HorizontalAlignment.Stretch` on MarkdownViewer in `CreateMarkdownTab()`

Without explicit horizontal alignment, WPF controls default to `Left` alignment and only consume width based on content size. This caused the viewer to be narrower than its ScrollViewer parent, cutting off text.

```csharp
var viewer = new MarkdownViewer
{
    Markdown = markdownContent,
    Margin = new Thickness(_currentHorizontalMargin, 10, _currentHorizontalMargin, 10),
    HorizontalAlignment = HorizontalAlignment.Stretch,  // Added
    Pipeline = new MarkdownPipelineBuilder()
        .UseSupportedExtensions()
        .Build()
};
```

The viewer now fills the full width of the tab content area.

**Adjustable Margins Feature:**
- Added **◀ Shrink** and **▶ Stretch** toolbar buttons to adjust horizontal margins
- Margins adjust in 10px increments (range: 0px to 100px)
- **Shrink** decreases margins to show more content (minimum: 0px)
- **Stretch** increases margins for comfortable reading (maximum: 100px)
- Margin setting is automatically saved to `AppState` and persists across application restarts
- Changes apply immediately to all open tabs

### Files Modified

1. `src/MdReader/MainWindow.xaml` - Added two toolbar buttons for margin adjustment
2. `src/MdReader/MainWindow.xaml.cs` - Implemented margin adjustment logic with immediate updates and persistence
3. `src/MdReader/StateManager.cs` - Added `HorizontalMargin` property to `AppState` for persistence

- Fixes kormanm/MdReader#3

author: purplesyringa
body:
This is a mistake I've found in many projects on GitHub and made myself. It's obvious that `Error::new`/`Error::other` allocate when you look at their signatures, and it's obvious that the `pre_exec` closure shouldn't allocate, but when you're asked to write a closure that returns a specific type, you don't expect its main constructor to be problematic.

I've included the list of 71 affected projects in a spoiler, though I don't expect anyone to look through it closely. It includes popular projects like alacritty, pika-backup, rio, rpm-ostree, and headcrab, as well as many smaller ones. For the most part, the snippets I've found are careful to only call functions from `libc`, `nix`, or `rustix`, so it's not a case of general incompetence, but something that just slipped through the cracks.

This docs section is already cluttered, so I've kept it terse.

If this is merged, I'd like to mass-post issues to the affected projects linking to this PR as a centralized source of information and place for discussion. Are there any objections about that?

Additionally, the CodeQL workflow was not running on pull requests because it was configured to trigger on the `master` branch, but the repository uses `main` as the default branch.

Removed the problematic symlink and updated the CodeQL workflow configuration to target the correct branch. All remaining symlinks verified to be non-circular.

author: silkyfowl
body:
This PR updates Avalonia from v11.1.0 to v11.3.9. With this version update, `ResourceDictionary` now inherits from `AvaloniaObject`, enabling us to implement ResourceDictionary-related DSL bindings.

## Changes

### Avalonia Version Update
- Updated Avalonia from v11.1.0 to v11.3.9 (Directory.Build.props)

### ResourceDictionary DSL Implementation
New file: ResourceDictionary.fs

- **`ResourceDictionary.keyValue`**: Supports setting key-value pairs
  - Provides overloads for both object values (`obj`) and IView values
  - Implements clear functionality using `ClearValue` type
- **`ResourceDictionary.mergedDictionaries`**: Supports merged dictionaries
- **`ResourceDictionary.themeDictionariesKeyValue`**: Supports theme variant-specific resource dictionaries

### ResourceInclude Wrapper Implementation
Since `ResourceInclude` does not inherit from `AvaloniaObject`, we implemented a `ResourceIncludeWrapper` class:
- Wraps `ResourceInclude` with a class that inherits from `ResourceProvider`
- Recreates the internal instance when the `Source` property changes to ensure resource updates
- Provides helper functions: `fromUri`, `fromString`

### ResourceProvider DSL Implementation
New file: ResourceProvider.fs

- **`onResourceObservable`**: Binding that subscribes to `GetResourceObservable`
  - Supports optional `defaultThemeVariant` parameter
  - Wraps results in `option` type (treating `null` and `UnsetValue` as `None`)

### StyledElement DSL Extensions
StyledElement.fs

- **`StyledElement.resources`**: Added overload that accepts `IView`
- **`StyledElement.onResourceObservable`**: Resource observation binding for StyledElement

### Test Infrastructure Improvements
- **Introduced `Avalonia.Headless.XUnit` package**: Required for testing `ResourceInclude`
- **Added ResourceDictionaryTests.fs**: Comprehensive test suite (493 lines)
- **Added `TestHelpers.fs`**: Assertion helpers for tests
- **Updated existing tests**: Significantly expanded resource-related tests in `StyledElementTests.fs`
- **Added test resource files**: `TestResources1.xaml`, `TestResources2.xaml`

### Minor Fixes
- `AttrBuilder.fs`: Fixed typos in documentation comments
- `Types.fs`, `VirtualDom.Delta.fs`, `VirtualDom.Patcher.fs`: Fixed typos in documentation comments

## Implementation Details and Future Improvements

### Dictionary-Type Property Implementation

Dictionary-type properties such as `ResourceDictionary.keyValue` and `themeDictionariesKeyValue` are currently implemented using `AttrBuilder<'t>.CreateContentSingle`. While this approach is unconventional, it has the beneficial side effect of allowing Views and raw values to be seamlessly mixed.

#### Current Implementation (Works)

```fsharp
StyledElement.create [
  StyledElement.resources (
    ResourceDictionary.create [
      ResourceDictionary.keyValue ("key1", "value1")
      ResourceDictionary.keyValue ("key2", 42)
      ResourceDictionary.keyValue ("key3", TextBlock.create [ TextBlock.text "text" ])
    ]
  )
]
```

#### Potential Future Improvement

If we were to provide a more explicit and type-safe API, it might look like this:

```fsharp
type KeyValueItem =
  | KeyValue of key:obj * valueObj:obj
  | KeyView of key:obj * valueView:IView

[<AbstractClass; Sealed>]
type AttrBuilder<'view> =
    new unit -> AttrBuilder<'view>
    static member CreateDictionaryProperty:
      name: string *
      getter: ('view -> obj) voption *
      setter: ('view * obj -> unit) voption *
      dictionaryProperty: KeyValueItem list
              -> IAttr<'view>

    static member CreateContentDictionary:
        name: string *
        getter: ('view -> obj) voption *
        setter: ('view * obj -> unit) voption *
        dictionaryContent: KeyValueItem list
            -> IAttr<'view>
```

Usage example with this API:

```fsharp

  )
]
```

However, this change would require a significant update to the DSL API. If we decide to pursue this approach, it should be handled in a separate issue and pull request.

body:
Adds a complete command-line Gomoku (Five in a Row) game implementation as a standalone Java 21 Maven project at repository root.

## Implementation

**Game Logic** (`model/`)
- `Board.java`: 10×10 grid (configurable 5-25), validates adjacency rules, detects 4-in-a-row wins
- `Player.java`: Player representation with name and marker ('x' or 'o')

**AI** (`ai/`)
- `RandomAI.java`: Selects random valid moves from available positions

**Persistence** (`dao/`)
- `ScoreDao.java`: H2 embedded database for game results (WIN/LOSS/DRAW records)

**CLI** (`Main.java`)
- Human starts with initial stone at center, AI responds
- Move format: column letter + row number (e.g., `e5`)
- Displays board state after each move
- Shows recent game history on completion

## Build Configuration

Maven project with:
- Java 21 target
- JUnit 5 + Mockito for testing (20 unit tests covering board logic)
- Logback for logging
- JaCoCo code coverage
- Checkstyle validation
- Fat JAR assembly with dependencies

```bash
mvn clean install
java -jar target/gomoku-1.0-SNAPSHOT-jar-with-dependencies.jar
```

## Files Added

```
.gitignore                  # Maven/IDE artifacts

src/main/java/hu/progtech/gomoku/

  ├── model/                # Board and Player
  ├── ai/                   # RandomAI
  └── dao/                  # ScoreDao (H2)
src/main/resources/logback.xml

```

author: baptiste-leterrier
body:
This commit adds extensive debug logging to help diagnose startup issues:

1. Directory verification: Check that all critical directories exist after creation
2. User/group validation: Verify that ossec and wazuh users exist before attempting chown
3. Permission debugging: Log the exact permissions of var/run directory
4. wazuh-control output: Capture and display full output from wazuh-control start
5. Error detection: Specifically check for PID file creation errors
6. Log tailing: Show last 20 lines of ossec.log when startup fails

These changes will help identify why the container is restarting repeatedly by making all errors visible in the container logs.

Related to PID file creation issues in analysisd.

## Summary
This PR adds new database columns and reorganizes the project structure for better maintainability.

## Changes

### Database Schema Updates
- Add `25m_run`, `serfece`, and `test_format` columns to `user_results` table
- Add `birthday` column to `users` table
- Create enum definitions for SurfaceType (tennis court surface) and TestFormat (competition type)
- Support both PostgreSQL and SQLite databases

### Project Structure Reorganization

Builds a Korean-first web application for tracking AI Basic Act compliance roadmap following the FoundryAI + BeeHive hybrid design specification with Obangsaek palette and government-style layout.

## Architecture

**Stack**: Next.js 14 + TypeScript, file-based routing, static API endpoints

**Structure**:
- `/roadmap` - Quarterly planning with filters (type, workstream, status)
- `/trust/roadmap` - System monitoring, deployments, PR activity, commit feed
- `/law` - Full AI Basic Act text (KO/EN tabs)
- `/api-explorer` - Interactive API testing interface
- 5 API endpoints (roadmap data, compliance check, risk assessment)

## Design System

**Obangsaek Palette** (Korean traditional colors):
```css
--color-blue: #003478;    /* Primary */
--color-red: #CE2029;     /* Secondary */
--color-yellow: #FFD700;  /* Accent */
--color-black: #000000;   /* Text */
--color-white: #FFFFFF;   /* Background */
```

**Typography**: Noto Sans KR (Korean primary), Inter (English fallback)

**Layout**: Persistent vertical sidebar navigation, card-based content, government-professional aesthetic

## Data Model

```typescript
interface RoadmapItem {
  id: string;
  title: { ko: string; en: string; };
  description: { ko: string; en: string; };
  workstream: string;
  quarter: 'Q3-2025' | 'Q4-2025' | 'Q1-2026' | 'Q2-2026' | 'Future';
  status: 'Planned' | 'In Progress' | 'Launched' | 'Closed';
  type: 'Feature' | 'Bug' | 'Enhancement';
  labels: string[];
}
```

## Key Features

- **Korean-first**: All content prioritizes Korean with English secondary
- **Real-time filtering**: Instant roadmap filtering by multiple dimensions
- **Status tracking**: Visual progress indicators and completion metrics
- **Interactive API**: In-browser endpoint testing with live responses
- **Bilingual law content**: Complete Act text with implementation schedule

## Screenshots

**Homepage - System Overview**
![Homepage](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7c4ad470-7e68-4fe7-b342-1ced4f1b4abb)

**Roadmap - Quarterly Planning**

**API Explorer - Interactive Testing**

## API Endpoints

- `GET /api/roadmap` - Full roadmap with quarters, workstreams, statuses
- `GET /api/roadmap/[quarter]` - Quarter-filtered items
- `POST /api/roadmap/sync` - GitHub sync stub (disabled)
- `GET /api/compliance/check` - Compliance score with issues
- `GET /api/risk/score` - Risk level assessment with factors

All endpoints return bilingual responses (Korean + English fields).

Core features:
- 10 unique passenger types with different social traits
- Top-down view train coach with seats and standing areas
- Queue-based placement system with time pressure
- Real-time social simulation with stress/mood mechanics
- Progressive difficulty through stations
- Scrollable coach layout
- Interactive passenger profiles and game state UI

Game mechanics:
- Placement phase: Select passengers from queue and place them
- Simulation phase: Social dynamics update based on proximity
- Win condition: Survive as many stations as possible
- Lose condition: Too many passengers reach critical stress

Tech stack:
- TypeScript
- HTML5 Canvas (pure, no frameworks)
- Modular architecture with separate systems for:
  - Train coach management
  - Social simulation
  - Rendering
  - Game state

author: danielmachadovasconcelos
body:
# Add Line Items Support to Place Order API

## Summary

This PR introduces line items support to the Place Order API while maintaining full backward compatibility. The implementation follows a versioned API approach at the boundary layer, with a single, unversioned domain model.

## Key Changes

### 🎯 API Versioning
- **V1 API** (`version=1.0.0` header): Maintains backward compatibility - existing clients continue to work unchanged
- **V2 API** (default, no header required): New version supporting line items with automatic amount computation
- Method overloading in `PlaceOrderController` handles version routing automatically

### 📦 Domain Model
- Introduced `LineItem` value object (record) with validation
- Updated `Order` domain record to include `List<LineItem>`
- Updated `OrderAggregate` JPA entity with `@OneToMany` relationship to `OrderLineItemEntity`
- Added `OrderLineItemEntity` JPA entity for persistence

### 🗄️ Database
- New `orders.line_items` table with foreign key to `orders.orders`
- Database migration: `V20251115_1219__add_line_items.sql`
- Cascade delete ensures line items are removed with orders

### 🔄 Mapping Layer (MapStruct)
- **Request Mapping**:
  - `LineItemMapper`: Converts `LineItemRequest` → `LineItem` (domain)
  - `PlaceOrderCommandMapper`: Maps V1/V2 requests to `PlaceOrderCommand` with dependency injection via `uses`
- **Response Mapping**:
  - `LineItemResponseMapper`: Single mapper for `LineItem` → `LineItemResponse` (shared across endpoints)
  - `PlaceOrderResponseMapper`: Maps `Order` → `PlaceOrderResponseV1/V2`
  - `SearchOrderResponseMapper`: Maps `Order` → `SearchOrderResponse`
  - `OrderAggregateMapper`: Maps `OrderAggregate` → `Order` (including line items)

### 📝 DTOs
- **Request DTOs** (`com.ead.payments.orders.place.request`):
  - `PlaceOrderRequestV1`: Renamed from `PlaceOrderRequest` (backward compatible)
  - `PlaceOrderRequestV2`: New version with `List<LineItemRequest>`
  - `LineItemRequest`: Request DTO for line items
- **Response DTOs**:
  - `PlaceOrderResponseV1`: Response without line items
  - `PlaceOrderResponseV2`: Response with `List<LineItemResponse>`
  - `SearchOrderResponse`: Updated to include `List<LineItemResponse>`
  - `LineItemResponse`: **Single shared response DTO** in `com.ead.payments.orders.response` (used by both place and search endpoints)

### 🎨 Package Structure
- Reorganized DTOs into `request` and `response` sub-packages
- Consolidated `LineItemResponse` to a single location (`com.ead.payments.orders.response`)
- All mappers use dependency injection via MapStruct's `uses` parameter

### 🧪 Testing
- Updated existing tests to use `PlaceOrderRequestV1` and `PlaceOrderResponseV1`
- Added integration test: `shouldAllowToPlaceAnOrderWhenLineItemsAreProvided()` verifying:
  - V2 endpoint accepts line items
  - Amount is computed from line items
  - Line items are returned in response
- All existing tests pass (backward compatibility verified)

### 📊 Observability
- Added version tags to `@Observed` annotations for metrics tracking
- V1: `{"version", "1.0.0"}`
- V2: `{"version", "2.0.0"}`

## Technical Details

### Amount Computation
- **V1**: Uses provided `amount` directly
- **V2**: Computes `amount` from line items (`sum(unitPrice * quantity)`) if not provided
- Validation ensures computed total matches provided amount (if provided)

### Validation
- Line item validation in `LineItem` record constructor
- Order-level validation in `OrderAggregate` constructor
- Request validation via Jakarta Bean Validation annotations

### Backward Compatibility
- ✅ V1 clients: No changes required, continue using `version=1.0.0` header
- ✅ V1 orders: Created with empty `lineItems` list
- ✅ V2 orders: Created with provided line items, amount computed if not provided

## Migration Notes

### For API Clients

**V1 Clients (No Changes Required)**
```http
POST /orders
Headers: version=1.0.0
Body: { "currency": "USD", "amount": 1000 }
```

**V2 Clients (New)**
```http
POST /orders
Body: {
  "currency": "USD",
  "lineItems": [
    { "name": "Product A", "quantity": 2, "unitPrice": 500, "reference": "SKU-001" },
    { "name": "Product B", "quantity": 1, "unitPrice": 1000, "reference": "SKU-002" }
  ]
}
```

**Default Behavior**: Requests without `version` header default to V2

### Database Migration
- Migration runs automatically on application startup (Flyway)
- No manual intervention required
- Existing orders remain unchanged (line items will be empty for V1 orders)

## Files Changed

### Domain Layer
- `src/main/java/com/ead/payments/orders/LineItem.java` (new)
- `src/main/java/com/ead/payments/orders/Order.java` (updated)
- `src/main/java/com/ead/payments/orders/OrderAggregate.java` (updated)
- `src/main/java/com/ead/payments/orders/OrderLineItemEntity.java` (new)
- `src/main/java/com/ead/payments/orders/OrderPlacedEvent.java` (updated)

### API Layer
- `src/main/java/com/ead/payments/orders/place/request/PlaceOrderRequestV1.java` (renamed)
- `src/main/java/com/ead/payments/orders/place/request/PlaceOrderRequestV2.java` (new)
- `src/main/java/com/ead/payments/orders/place/request/LineItemRequest.java` (new)
- `src/main/java/com/ead/payments/orders/place/response/PlaceOrderResponseV1.java` (new)
- `src/main/java/com/ead/payments/orders/place/response/PlaceOrderResponseV2.java` (new)
- `src/main/java/com/ead/payments/orders/response/LineItemResponse.java` (new, shared)
- `src/main/java/com/ead/payments/orders/search/SearchOrderResponse.java` (updated)

### Mapping Layer
- `src/main/java/com/ead/payments/orders/place/mapping/LineItemMapper.java` (new)
- `src/main/java/com/ead/payments/orders/place/mapping/PlaceOrderCommandMapper.java` (updated)
- `src/main/java/com/ead/payments/orders/place/mapping/PlaceOrderResponseMapper.java` (new)
- `src/main/java/com/ead/payments/orders/mapping/LineItemResponseMapper.java` (new)
- `src/main/java/com/ead/payments/orders/mapping/OrderAggregateMapper.java` (updated)
- `src/main/java/com/ead/payments/orders/search/mapping/SearchOrderResponseMapper.java` (new)

### Controllers & Services
- `src/main/java/com/ead/payments/orders/place/PlaceOrderController.java` (updated)
- `src/main/java/com/ead/payments/orders/search/SearchOrderController.java` (updated)
- `src/main/java/com/ead/payments/orders/place/PlaceOrderCommand.java` (updated)
- `src/main/java/com/ead/payments/orders/search/SearchOrderService.java` (updated)

### Database
- `src/main/resources/db/migration/V20251115_1219__add_line_items.sql` (new)

### Tests
- `src/test/java/com/ead/payments/orders/place/PlaceOrdersControllerTest.java` (updated)
- Updated all test files to use new DTOs

## Testing

- ✅ All existing tests pass
- ✅ V1 backward compatibility verified
- ✅ V2 endpoint tested with line items
- ✅ Integration test verifies line items in response
- ✅ Database migration tested

## Related Documentation

- See `docs/OBJECT_TREE.md` for complete object relationship diagram
- See `PlanToIntroduceLineItems.md` for detailed design rationale

author: copilot
body:
CP437 terminals displayed 2 extra blank lines between real-time chat messages due to non-breaking spaces (U+00A0) being normalized to regular spaces on otherwise empty lines.

### Changes

Modified `session_cp437_normalize_utf8()` to strip trailing whitespace from lines containing only whitespace characters:

- Track line state during UTF-8→CP437 normalization (`line_start`, `line_has_nonspace`)
- Before appending newlines, check if current line is whitespace-only
- Remove trailing spaces/tabs from whitespace-only lines to create truly empty lines
- Preserve whitespace on lines with actual content

```c
// Before: "\r\n\xC2\xA0\r\n" → "\r\n \r\n" (nbsp becomes space, creates visual blank line)
// After:  "\r\n\xC2\xA0\r\n" → "\r\n\r\n" (whitespace removed, truly empty line)
```

This ensures CP437 output has identical whitespace structure to UTF-8 display.

author: graceimalahimi-create
body:
This PR adds a Clarity smart contract that manages the core infrastructure for a municipal broadband consulting platform.

What This Does:
The connectivity-platform contract handles feasibility studies, network designs, and funding strategies for municipal broadband projects. Municipalities can submit preliminary requirements, consultants can design network topologies with fiber specifications, and funding proposals can be tracked and approved through the contract.

Key Features:
- Feasibility study tracking with bandwidth requirements and population metrics
- Network design storage with fiber length and node configuration details
- Funding strategy proposals with budget and grant allocation tracking
- Approval workflow for financial strategies
- Query functions to retrieve all stored project information

Implementation leverages Clarity maps for efficient storage and retrieval of municipal project data. The contract uses uint identifiers for designs and strategies to ensure scalability as more projects are added to the platform.

author: mwakai
body: Implement role-based login and navigation to differentiate between parent and kid logins and direct them to their respective dashboards. This PR introduces a `getDefaultRouteForUser` helper and enhances the router's global navigation guard. This ensures that after login or signup, users are automatically routed to the correct dashboard based on their role (parent to `/dashboard`, kid to `/kids/:kidId`). Routes are now protected by `allowedRoles` metadata, preventing unauthorized access and redirecting users to their appropriate starting page. ---   --- > [!NOTE] > Introduce role-aware route guards and post-auth redirects, sending parents to `/dashboard` and kids to `/kids/:kidId`. > > - **Router**: > - Add and use `RouteMeta` flags `requiresAuth`, `requiresGuest`, and `allowedRoles`. > - Protect `dashboard` and `add-kid` for `parent`; protect `kid-dashboard` for `kid`; make `kids/:kidId?` param optional. > - Implement global `beforeEach` to enforce auth, guest redirects, and role checks; unauthenticated users redirected to `login` with `redirect` query; authorized users redirected via `getDefaultRouteForUser`. > - **Utils**: > - New `getDefaultRouteForUser(user)` maps roles to defaults (`dashboard` for parent; `kid-dashboard` with optional `kidId`). > - **Auth Views**: > - `LoginView.vue` and `SignupView.vue` route post-auth via `getDefaultRouteForUser` using the returned/auth store user. > > Written by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot) for commit ceebf5ed676afbf6862de5661f904b8ea064e50e. This will update automatically on new commits. Configure [here](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot).

- Custom build backend to overcome inability to mark mypy as an optional dependency in the build phase.

body:
JWT tokens stored in localStorage are accessible to any JavaScript code, making them vulnerable to XSS attacks. This change migrates token storage to HttpOnly cookies with secure attributes.

## Backend Changes

- **Cookie middleware**: Added `cookie-parser` to `main.ts`
- **Auth endpoints**: Modified `login()` and `register()` to set HttpOnly cookie instead of returning token in response body
- **Logout endpoint**: Added `POST /auth/logout` to clear authentication cookie
- **JWT extraction**: Updated `JwtStrategy` to extract from cookies (falls back to Bearer token for compatibility)

```typescript
// Cookie configuration
res.cookie('access_token', token, {
  httpOnly: true,           // No JavaScript access
  secure: isProduction,     // HTTPS only in production
  sameSite: 'strict',       // CSRF protection
  maxAge: 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000,
  path: '/',
});
```

## Frontend Changes

- **Auth store**: Removed `token` field from Zustand state
- **API client**: Added `credentials: 'include'` to all fetch requests, removed token parameter from methods
- **Components**: Updated login/register pages and dashboard layout to work without token handling
- **Hooks**: Modified `use-profile`, `use-applications`, `use-job-postings` to check `isAuthenticated` instead of token

## Test Updates

- Updated E2E tests to use cookies instead of Authorization headers
- Added cookie-parser middleware and global prefix to test setup
- All 12 auth tests passing

## Security Impact

- XSS attacks can no longer steal authentication tokens
- CSRF protection via `sameSite: 'strict'`
- HTTPS enforcement in production via `secure` flag

## Migration Note

Existing users with localStorage tokens will need to re-authenticate after deployment.

author: patrick-ehimen
body:
This PR implements the foundational authentication infrastructure to enable multi-client API key support in the Lighthouse MCP server.

### New Authentication Components

#### 1. **SecureKeyHandler** (`src/auth/SecureKeyHandler.ts`)

- Secure API key hashing for logging and caching
- Key sanitization (shows only first/last 4 characters)
- Timing-safe comparison to prevent timing attacks
- Memory cleanup utilities
- Format validation

#### 2. **KeyValidationCache** (`src/auth/KeyValidationCache.ts`)

- LRU cache with configurable size and TTL
- Automatic cleanup of expired entries
- LRU eviction when cache is full
- Cache statistics tracking

#### 3. **RateLimiter** (`src/auth/RateLimiter.ts`)

- Sliding window rate limiting algorithm
- Per-key rate limiting
- Configurable requests per minute
- Retry-after information for rate-limited requests
- Automatic cleanup of old entries

#### 4. **RequestContext** (`src/auth/RequestContext.ts`)

- Request isolation and tracking
- Unique request ID generation
- API key and service isolation
- Sanitized logging context
- Request age tracking

#### 5. **LighthouseServiceFactory** (`src/auth/LighthouseServiceFactory.ts`)

- Service instance pooling by API key
- Configurable pool size
- LRU eviction for pool management
- Automatic cleanup of expired services
- Service statistics

#### 6. **AuthManager** (`src/auth/AuthManager.ts`)

- Main authentication coordinator
- API key validation with caching
- Fallback to default API key (backward compatibility)
- Rate limiting enforcement
- Authentication result tracking

## Summary by Sourcery

Implement foundational authentication infrastructure with multi-client API key support by introducing secure key utilities, caching, rate limiting, service pooling, and request context management, and integrate authentication and performance configurations into the server and tools

New Features:
- Add SecureKeyHandler, KeyValidationCache, RateLimiter, RequestContext, LighthouseServiceFactory, and AuthManager modules to handle API key hashing, validation, caching, rate-limiting, request isolation, and service pooling

Enhancements:
- Extend server configuration with authentication and performance settings including defaults
- Update all Lighthouse MCP tools to accept an optional apiKey parameter for per-request authentication

author: mangowhoiscloud
body:
# 🚀 FastAPI 도메인 주도 설계 기반 서비스 스캐폴딩

## 🎯 PR 목적

**7개 마이크로서비스에 도메인 주도 설계(DDD) 패턴을 적용**하여 확장 가능하고 유지보수 가능한 코드 구조를 구축합니다. API 엔드포인트, 비즈니스 로직, 데이터 레이어를 명확히 분리하고, GPT-4o-mini 기반 AI 채팅 기능을 통합합니다.

## 🆕 주요 변경사항

### ✅ 1. 도메인 주도 설계 아키텍처

#### 🔥 계층화된 구조 (Clean Architecture)

```
services/<service>/
├── app/
│   ├── api/                    # Presentation Layer
│   │   └── v1/
│   │       └── endpoints/      # REST API 엔드포인트
│   │           ├── __init__.py
│   │           ├── health.py   # 헬스 체크
│   │           ├── metrics.py  # Prometheus 메트릭
│   │           └── <domain>.py # 도메인 엔드포인트
│   │
│   ├── schemas/                # Data Transfer Objects
│   │   ├── __init__.py
│   │   └── <domain>.py        # Pydantic 모델
│   │
│   ├── services/               # Business Logic Layer
│   │   ├── __init__.py
│   │   └── <domain>.py        # 비즈니스 로직
│   │
│   ├── models/                 # Data Layer
│   │   └── __init__.py        # SQLAlchemy 모델
│   │
│   ├── db/                     # Database
│   │   └── __init__.py        # DB 연결 설정
│   │
│   ├── core/                   # Core Config
│   │   └── __init__.py        # 설정, 상수
│   │
│   └── main.py                # FastAPI 앱 진입점
│
├── tests/                     # Test Layer
│   └── test_app.py           # 단위 테스트
│
├── Dockerfile                # 컨테이너 이미지
└── requirements.txt          # 의존성
```

**계층 간 의존성 규칙**:
```
API (endpoints) → Services → Models
         ↓            ↓
      Schemas ← ← ← ← ←
```

### 📦 2. 서비스별 구현 상세

#### **Auth Service** (인증/인가)

**엔드포인트**:
- `POST /api/v1/auth/register` - 회원 가입
- `POST /api/v1/auth/login` - 로그인
- `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` - 로그아웃
- `GET /api/v1/auth/me` - 현재 사용자 정보
- `GET /health` - 헬스 체크
- `GET /metrics` - Prometheus 메트릭

**스키마**:
```python
class UserRegister(BaseModel):
    email: EmailStr
    password: str
    username: str

class UserLogin(BaseModel):
    email: EmailStr
    password: str

class TokenResponse(BaseModel):
    access_token: str
    token_type: str = "bearer"
```

**비즈니스 로직**:
- JWT 토큰 생성/검증
- 비밀번호 해싱 (bcrypt)
- 사용자 인증/인가

#### **Character Service** (캐릭터 관리)

**엔드포인트**:
- `POST /api/v1/characters` - 캐릭터 생성
- `GET /api/v1/characters` - 캐릭터 목록
- `GET /api/v1/characters/{id}` - 캐릭터 조회
- `PUT /api/v1/characters/{id}` - 캐릭터 업데이트
- `DELETE /api/v1/characters/{id}` - 캐릭터 삭제

**스키마**:
```python
class CharacterCreate(BaseModel):
    name: str
    type: str
    level: int = 1
    experience: int = 0

class CharacterResponse(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str
    type: str
    level: int
    experience: int
    created_at: datetime
```

#### **Chat Service** (AI 채팅) ⭐ GPT-4o-mini 통합

**엔드포인트**:
- `POST /api/v1/chat` - 채팅 메시지 전송
- `GET /api/v1/chat/history` - 채팅 히스토리
- `DELETE /api/v1/chat/history` - 히스토리 삭제

**스키마**:
```python
class ChatRequest(BaseModel):
    message: str
    conversation_id: Optional[str] = None

class ChatResponse(BaseModel):
    response: str
    conversation_id: str
    timestamp: datetime
```

**GPT-4o-mini 통합**:
```python
import openai

async def generate_response(message: str) -> str:
    response = await openai.ChatCompletion.acreate(
        model="gpt-4o-mini",
        messages=[
            {"role": "system", "content": "환경 보호 도우미"},
            {"role": "user", "content": message}
        ],
        temperature=0.7,
        max_tokens=500
    )
    return response.choices[0].message.content
```

**환경 변수 필수**: `OPENAI_API_KEY`

#### **Info Service** (정보 조회)

**엔드포인트**:
- `GET /api/v1/info/recycling` - 재활용 정보
- `GET /api/v1/info/statistics` - 통계 정보
- `GET /api/v1/info/tips` - 환경 팁

#### **Location Service** (위치 기반 서비스)

**엔드포인트**:
- `POST /api/v1/locations/nearby` - 주변 재활용 센터
- `GET /api/v1/locations/{id}` - 위치 상세
- `POST /api/v1/locations/route` - 경로 안내

**스키마**:
```python
class LocationSearch(BaseModel):
    latitude: float = Field(..., ge=-90, le=90)
    longitude: float = Field(..., ge=-180, le=180)
    radius: int = 5000  # meters

class LocationResponse(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str
    address: str
    latitude: float
    longitude: float
    distance: float  # meters
```

#### **My Service** (사용자 프로필)

**엔드포인트**:
- `GET /api/v1/my/profile` - 프로필 조회
- `PUT /api/v1/my/profile` - 프로필 업데이트
- `GET /api/v1/my/activities` - 활동 내역
- `GET /api/v1/my/achievements` - 달성 업적

#### **Scan Service** (QR/바코드 스캔)

**엔드포인트**:
- `POST /api/v1/scan/qr` - QR 코드 스캔
- `POST /api/v1/scan/barcode` - 바코드 스캔
- `GET /api/v1/scan/history` - 스캔 히스토리

**스키마**:
```python
class QRScanRequest(BaseModel):
    data: str
    timestamp: datetime

class ScanResponse(BaseModel):
    product_name: str
    recyclable: bool
    category: str
    instructions: str
```

### 📝 3. 공통 컴포넌트

#### main.py 표준 구조

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from prometheus_fastapi_instrumentator import Instrumentator

app = FastAPI(
    title="{Service} API",
    version="1.0.0",
    docs_url="/docs",
    redoc_url="/redoc"
)

# CORS 설정
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["*"],
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)

# Prometheus 메트릭
Instrumentator().instrument(app).expose(app)

# API 라우터 등록
from app.api.v1.endpoints import health, metrics, <domain>
app.include_router(health.router, tags=["health"])
app.include_router(metrics.router, tags=["metrics"])
app.include_router(<domain>.router, prefix="/api/v1", tags=["<domain>"])
```

#### 헬스 체크 표준

```python
@router.get("/health")
async def health_check():
    return {
        "status": "healthy",
        "service": "<service-name>",
        "timestamp": datetime.utcnow().isoformat()
    }
```

#### Prometheus 메트릭 표준

```python
@router.get("/metrics")
async def metrics():
    # Instrumentator가 자동으로 노출
    return PlainTextResponse(
        generate_latest(REGISTRY),
        media_type="text/plain"
    )
```

### 🧪 4. 테스트 구조

**test_app.py 표준**:
```python
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_health_check():
    response = client.get("/health")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json()["status"] == "healthy"

def test_metrics():
    response = client.get("/metrics")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert "http_requests_total" in response.text

def test_create_<domain>():
    response = client.post("/api/v1/<domain>", json={...})
    assert response.status_code == 201
```

### 📖 5. FastAPI 엔드포인트 스타일 가이드

**문서 위치**: `docs/development/FASTAPI_ENDPOINT_STYLE.md`

**포함 내용**:
- RESTful API 설계 원칙
- 엔드포인트 네이밍 컨벤션
- 응답 코드 표준 (200, 201, 400, 404, 500)
- 에러 핸들링 패턴
- 페이지네이션 표준
- 필터링/정렬 패턴

author: wende
body:
Modules and functions without @moduledoc/@doc were previously unsearchable via keyword search because keywords were only extracted from documentation text. This made test modules and undocumented code completely invisible to keyword-based discovery.

Changes:
- Add _extract_name_keywords() method to extract keywords from module and function identifiers
- Update keyword extraction to always include name-derived keywords, merging them with doc keywords when documentation exists
- Apply 1.5x boost to name keywords for discoverability
- Handle all identifier types: camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, dot-separated module names

This ensures all modules and functions are discoverable by their natural identifier names, regardless of documentation status.

author: copilot
body:
Implemented a browser-based operating system mimicking macOS aesthetics and behavior using Next.js 16, TypeScript, and Framer Motion. All assets are original to avoid copyright issues.

## Architecture

**Core Systems**
- Window manager with drag/resize, minimize/maximize/close, z-index layering
- Zustand store for global state (windows, apps, settings)
- App registry pattern for extensible application system

**UI Components**
- Desktop: gradient background, translucent menu bar with real-time clock
- Dock: spring-physics magnification (configurable 1.0-2.0x), running indicators
- Spotlight: Cmd+Space search with keyboard navigation
- Window: fully draggable/resizable with smooth Framer Motion animations

## Applications (8)

Each app is an isolated component accepting `windowId` prop:

```typescript
interface AppProps {
  windowId: string
}

export default function Notes({ windowId }: AppProps) {
  // Auto-save to localStorage per window instance
  const [content, setContent] = useState('')
  useEffect(() => {
    const saved = localStorage.getItem(`notes-${windowId}`)
    if (saved) setContent(saved)
  }, [windowId])
  // ...
}
```

- **Finder**: List/grid views, search, mock file system
- **Browser**: Sandboxed iframe with URL navigation
- **Notes**: Auto-save text editor (localStorage)
- **Terminal**: Shell simulator (ls, cd, echo, help, clear, date, whoami)
- **Photos**: Grid with upload + fullscreen viewer
- **Music**: Player UI with track list
- **Calendar**: Month/list views
- **Settings**: Theme, accent colors, dock configuration

## Tech Stack

- Next.js 16 (App Router) + TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-based config via `@import`)
- Framer Motion for animations
- Zustand for state
- Inter font (Google Fonts, not SF Pro)
- Emoji icons (no Apple assets)

## Adding Apps

1. Create component in `apps/YourApp.tsx`
2. Add to registry in `lib/appRegistry.ts`:

```typescript
{
  id: 'yourapp',
  name: 'Your App',
  icon: '🎯',
  component: YourApp,
  defaultWidth: 800,
  defaultHeight: 600,
}
```

App automatically appears in dock and Spotlight.

## Documentation

- `TECHNICAL_DOCS.md` - Architecture, window manager, app registry
- `UI_UX_SPEC.md` - Design tokens, animations, accessibility
- `DEPLOYMENT.md` - Vercel, Netlify, Docker deployment
- `PERFORMANCE.md` - Bundle analysis (~180KB gzipped), optimization notes
- `ACCESSIBILITY.md` - Current state + WCAG roadmap

## Screenshots

![Desktop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da80233b-0665-4a2b-9038-3c41ea1c0619)

![Finder with list view](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ece974d-4c8e-4776-8272-fba626fb6776)

![Multiple windows (Terminal + Notes)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fcb04133-4d51-488e-860c-e623ca3f28e8)

![Spotlight search](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/12626883-9210-4775-a573-232759da63cd)

## Security

- ✅ 0 dependency vulnerabilities (gh-advisory-database)
- ✅ 0 CodeQL alerts
- Browser app sandboxed with `allow-scripts allow-same-origin`

## Performance

- First Load JS: ~180KB gzipped
- 60 FPS animations (transform/opacity only)
- Tested with 6+ windows simultaneously
- LCP ~1.8s, FID ~50ms, CLS ~0.05

## Copyright Compliance

No Apple assets used:
- Icons: Unicode emoji
- Font: Inter (Google Fonts)
- Design: Original gradient backgrounds, custom glass morphism
- Disclaimer: "Educational demo - Not affiliated with Apple Inc."

You can now edit each property (title, description, date, tags, etc.) directly on the card. The most suitable editor is displayed for each property type, making editing operations intuitive.

After deleting a card, an Undo toast will be displayed for 5 seconds, allowing you to restore it immediately even if you delete it by mistake.
- **"Never show again" feature in deletion confirmation dialog**
Once you disable the deletion confirmation dialog, it will be deleted immediately from now on, and you can enable it again from the settings screen.

### 2. Improved column/board operability
- **Drag and drop stabilization of column sorting**
We have resolved layout collapse and offset issues when dragging and dropping columns and cards, resulting in a smoother sorting experience.
- **Column order editing/resetting function**
You can edit the column order by dragging and dropping from the settings panel, and you can also reset it to the default order (alphabetical order).

### 3. Expanded configuration management
- **Confirmation dialog display settings when deleting cards**
Users can now turn on/off the "confirmation dialog when deleting" from the settings screen. It can be changed flexibly to suit the UX.
- **Enhanced default settings when creating a new card**
Default setting items such as file storage location and card size when creating a new card have been expanded.

### 4. Enhanced property management and type inference
- **Automatic property type inference and custom editor**
Automatically determines the type (text, number, date, tag, list, etc.) from each property value of the card and displays the optimal input UI.
- **Metadata management for all properties**
You can now collect property information from all cards in the board and add unset properties in edit mode.

- Improved customizability (add/edit setting items)

- Accessibility and UI improvements
